changelogLatest.detail: RFP rows carry publishedBrief when SCF published one: its title, a commit-pinned copy of the RFP Track page and the day it was read (13 of 16 rows; none was found for concentrated-liquidity-amm, soroban-vrf or ai-webide). technicalRequirements is the idea's own summary. For contract-source-verification it differs from the brief, so publishedBrief restates the brief's functional requirements (the SEP-58 fields bldimg, bldopt, source_repo, source_rev, tarball_url and tarball_sha256, and an SDF-allowlisted trusted build image) and what it rules out (fully deterministic Rust compilation as a research effort). rules.rubric lists seven criteria scored 1 to 5 and weighted 20, 20, 15, 15, 10, 10 and 10 percent, from hackmeridian.com/build; the 20 percent slot, Track Alignment for Genesis and Ecosystem Alignment for Scale, names each in byCategory. reviewSubmission's judging carries the same rubric beside its criteria. An event off DoraHacks: meta.note no longer reports a DoraHacks feed outage; its winners come from its curated roster even before Scout's stored copy holds them (each row's url the page that names the win); rules absent means its record copies no judging sentence. The Istanbul event serves its two tracks, its judging sentence from Rise In's page and its seven winners from Rise In's recap, ranked; its dates are Istanbul's (the page header prints its local-midnight start in UTC, as 18 September). A DoraHacks roster that could not be read now serves submissions null with a note, and a successful read that found none keeps []. getHackathons: a DoraHacks listing read in part is a failed read (partial true, counts.total null); an empty upcoming or active feed says no event of that status is in this feed, names any q, organizer or source filter, and says when part of the feed could not be read, not that the ecosystem is between events. meta.quarters and meta.categories are declared as the {value, label} objects they always were. getRfps q also matches a row's published brief (its title, functional requirements and out-of-scope items): q=bldimg finds contract-source-verification. The skill no longer calls open briefs continuously fundable, nor says that no open match means no SCF round covers the lane: counts.open can be 0, and meta.scfRound says whether SCF takes submissions now. The curated feed's scope is Stellar-presented hackathons and university challenges off DoraHacks, and an empty upcoming or active feed says so. getHackathon rules: a page that publishes no judging criteria now says so in rules.judgingNote, with the page and the day (the 10 listed DoraHacks events whose page has no judging section, Stellar Hacks: Real-World ZK among them, and 5 curated events whose organizer page was checked on 2026-11-04), never a bare null. The page reader, which serves a DoraHacks event's stored page as it reads it now, finds a section under a line of its own or a bold label, in Spanish or Portuguese too; takes the event's own heading over a track's, and serves sections that sit under different tracks each under its track; reads a heading that names both sections by its labelled parts; and no longer reads a list of judges as criteria or Prerequisites as requirements. Over the 20 listed DoraHacks pages, read 2026-11-04: Stellar IdeaThon Mulheres Que Codam serves its criteria (Inovação e Originalidade, Melhor apresentação, Go to market, Qualidade Técnica) and its deliverables; buildonstellarchile, give-hackathon-argentina and stellar-latam gain their submission requirements; give-hackathon-argentina serves its criteria and its requirements apart, where one section served both; ideaton2026's requirements are its event-wide Rules, not one track's. getHackathon answers 503 (could not check) when a DoraHacks listing read failed and the slug was not found, never 404; a roster DoraHacks read as empty says so in stats.winnersNote rather than that it could not be read; a roster read cut short (the page cap, or fewer rows than its own count) is a failed read, never served as whole. Build on Stellar Philippines serves its weighted criteria as rules.rubric (impact 30, technical execution on Stellar 25, UX 20, innovation 15, feasibility 10 percent; no score scale published). reviewSubmission: categoryContext states its denominator (outOf, with uncategorized beside it), and a new eventCategories gives, for each event the submission entered, the event's stored submissions, how many are categorized, its five largest categories and this submission's category among them, counted by analyzeHackathonSubmissions' category facet; it is served even when the submission has no confident category, as dorahacks.io/buidl/42765 has none.
changelogLatest.summary: getRfps follows SCF's RFP Track page, which names no open brief now (Q4 2026 RFPs are coming soon): activeQuarter is q4-2026, counts.open is 0 and the two Q3 briefs read closed, and meta.briefRoster gives that page and the day it was read. getHackathon serves HackMeridian 2026's weighted rubric as rules.rubric and says what Scout holds of an event off DoraHacks: submissions is null when no roster is held or none could be read, never [] for a roster no read reached. getHackathons lists the Rise In Stellar Pro Hackathon in Istanbul (19 to 20 September 2026) with its seven winners, and the University of Waterloo's Blockchain Innovation Challenge powered by Stellar (2 to 18 November 2026, active now).

fields.description: Comma-separated top-level field names to return per row (e.g. fields=name,slug,tvlUSD), shrinking the payload. Case-insensitive. Each row's identity keys (id/slug/fullName/githubUsername/url/source, where present) are always included; unknown names are ignored, not rejected. Applies only to the rows array: meta is unaffected. Nested objects are selected whole (no dot-paths).
fields.name: fields

limit.description: Max results per page. The default and cap VARY by endpoint (e.g. projects/search 20/100, builders 50/200, leaderboard 50/300, research 8/25). A value below 1 or above the cap is clamped, not rejected.
limit.name: limit

offset.description: Number of matching rows to skip before returning (pagination). Page until offset + meta.counts.returned >= meta.counts.total.
offset.name: offset

view.description: Row shape. `full` (the default) returns every row field, unchanged. `compact` is for callers whose tool output is capped: each row is rebuilt from a fixed key list (identity, rank and score, and the fields that answer the usual question), and list fields left out come back as counts. A default projects/search page for q=lending measured 87,157 characters full and 23,091 compact (2026-10-23). Every compact row carries the same keys, null where there is no value; a field missing from a compact row was left out, not found empty. `meta.view` (first in meta) says the page is compact and where the left-out detail is read: repeat the request without view, or without view and with fields=<names>. The key lists are in the CompactView schema. Cannot be combined with fields (400). Any other value answers 400 with validValues.
view.name: view

Audit.description: One security-audit report row from the /api/audits registry. Null semantics: projectSlug null = the audited codebase has no directory project (NOT 'unaudited'); findingsTotal/severityCounts null = not extracted, NOT zero.

chunksIndexed.description: Full-text chunks serving this report via /api/research?source=audit

dateBasis.description: published = real date-stamp; portal-record = wall-clock portal timestamp (likely upload time); not publication recency; null = pre-dateBasis row

engagementEnd.description: Engagement window end as stated IN the report (YYYY-MM-DD).

engagementId.description: Relation metadata: shared by every report of ONE engagement, distinct across engagements; lets a consumer tell a revision from a separate yearly engagement. Null = unclassified (curation pending), never asserted independent.

engagementStart.description: Engagement window start as stated IN the report (YYYY-MM-DD).

findingsExtraction.description: Completeness of the deterministic findings extraction: read findingsTotal 7 vs null as different states of KNOWLEDGE, not conflicting counts. Null on rows ingested before this field existed.

findingsTotal.description: Populated when the auditor's report format parses deterministically AND round-trips its own stated count (OtterSec, Veridise, Certora, Code4rena, Hacken). null = not extracted, NOT zero.

linkBasis.description: Provenance of the project link: name-exact | alias | unmatched (verified no-match); null = not yet triaged

observedAt.description: When our crawler last saw the report live

projectSlug.description: Verified directory-project link; null = no directory project for this codebase (NOT 'unaudited')

reportVersion.description: Version the report states about itself (e.g. 'V2'); null when the source states none.

severityCounts.description: {critical, high, medium, low, informational} counts, only for formats carrying per-finding severity that agrees with its finding-ID prefix (Certora tables, Code4rena tier headings). null = not extracted, NOT zero.

supersededByReportId.description: reportId of the report that supersedes this one; null = no supersession stated by the documents (never guessed).

Builder.description: A builder profile row from /api/builders. Profile text (bio/roleTitle) is builder-claimed, NOT verified experience; when the request had a q/skill filter, `match` and `codeEvidence` carry the match provenance. Nullable profile fields are null (or empty-string) when unset; never a negative claim.

codeEvidence.description: Indexed repos owned by this builder's GitHub account that match the query: observable facts (language, last activity), kept SEPARATE from subjective profile text. [] = every repo in the index that this GitHub account owns was read and none matched (a weaker match, not a disqualification). Owners match as GitHub logins do, whole and in any case; repos GitHub reports gone are left out. null = not checked: no q/skill filter, or the code-evidence read failed (meta.failedReads names it), on every row including code-language ones; never 'none'.

displayName.description: Display name; falls back to githubUsername when unset.

githubUsername.description: Natural key; also the stellarlight.xyz/builders/{githubUsername} page slug.

location.description: Free-text location as entered (e.g. 'Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brasil'); the ?location= filter substring-matches this.

match.description: WHY this row matched (null without a q/skill filter). Free-text profile evidence: treat bio/role text as claims, not verified experience.

basis.description: 'profile-text' = free-text hit over a Stellar Passport builder's profile/project prose. 'repo-owner' = a CODE-DERIVED row: the query is a GitHub login that owns indexed Stellar repos but has no Passport profile, so bio/roleTitle are null and the evidence is entirely in codeEvidence (P2 builders-by-name). 'code-language' = admitted by CODE, not prose: at least one query token IS the primary language of a repo this builder owns in the index while their profile never says it (matchedFields INCLUDES 'codeEvidence', matchedTerms naming the language as indexed, proving repos in codeEvidence, null like every row when the code-evidence read failed); every other token still had to hit the prose, so a MIXED row (one token by code, another by prose) also lists the prose fields in matchedFields and still keeps the 'code-language' basis; these candidate rows sort below all prose hits.

matchedFields.description: Profile fields the query hit (bio, roleTitle, displayName, githubUsername, location, projects).

matchedProjects.description: Projects whose name/description matched the query.

matchedTerms.description: Per query token, the literal term that hit: a token can match via a synonym (e.g. 'payments' via 'remittance').

onStellar.description: What this person has actually shipped on Stellar, from the repos we index; QUERY-INDEPENDENT and present on every row (the profile page's 'On Stellar' card as data). Attribution rule: `builds` = projects reached through repos they OWN or an org that IS them; `contributesTo` = projects reached only through repos they committed to; `commits90d` counts OWN repos only; `contributedCommits12m` is their own share of others' repos; a repo's total is never credited to a contributor. `null` = the join could not run (never 'nothing'); an all-zero block = the join ran and found no indexed code for this login. `projects` above stays Passport-declared and `codeEvidence` stays query-scoped, unchanged.

commits90d.description: Commits in the last 90 days across repos this person OWNS.

contributedCommits12m.description: This person's own commits into repos they don't own, last 12 months (contributor pass).

languages.description: Primary languages across their indexed repos, most common first.

topRepos.description: Up to 5: owned repos first, then by this person's own commits, then the repo's 90d activity. Never ordered by the repo's total alone.

commits90d.description: The REPO's 90-day commits (everyone's work); context, not this person's count.

myCommits12m.description: This person's own commits into this repo, last 12 months; null for owned repos (their own repo; the whole history is theirs).

projectCount.description: Length of `projects`: the builder's own synced entries, not an ecosystem-wide attribution count.

projects.description: Projects synced from the builder's Stellar Passport profile. Raw sync rows: keys are snake_case, and extra passthrough fields (id, website_url, demo_url, docs_url, contract_address, repos, heatmap…) may ride along.

twitterHandle.description: As entered by the builder: can be a bare handle OR a full profile URL; normalize before constructing links.

url.description: Canonical builder profile page on stellarlight.xyz.

Cluster.description: One category/type cluster from /api/clusters: crowdedness/whitespace over the active project directory. size is a directory TAXONOMY count (how many projects carry the tag), NOT a venue or competitor count: the DEX cluster, e.g., includes aggregators and trading UIs alongside independent venues.

crowdedness.description: 1-10 log-scaled crowding score: round(log2(size+1) + log2(scfFundedCount+1) + 0.5*log2(hackathonWinnerCount+1)), clamped to 1..10. SCF funding and winners add a modifier, so a well-funded small cluster can outrank a huge unfunded one. Sort descending for 'most crowded', ascending for whitespace.

dimension.description: Which taxonomy this cluster was computed over (echoes ?dimension=).

hackathonWinnerCount.description: Cluster projects with a top hackathon placement.

key.description: The cluster label: a category (dimension=category) or a types[] value (dimension=types), e.g. 'RWA'.

sampleProjects.description: A few showcase projects, sorted by SCF funding + hackathon prize; a SAMPLE of the cluster, not its full membership (enumerate via searchProjects).

scfFundedCount.description: Cluster projects with an SCF award.

scfTotalUSD.description: Sum of known SCF award amounts across the cluster; an in-house reconstruction (per-award amounts aren't published for all rounds): comparable across clusters, not an official figure.

size.description: Projects in the cluster: a taxonomy count (see component description).

CompactView.description: Present in meta only when the request had view=compact; absent means full rows. Compact project rows (projects/search `projects`) carry exactly: id, name, slug, canonicalSlug, url, category, types, shortDescription, status, statusAsOf, deployment, tvlUSD, tvlAsOf, tvlStale, scfAwarded, scfTotalAwardedUSD, audits, score, via, confidence, reposCount, onchainContractsCount; deployment keeps only network, confidence only score and label. Compact repo rows (repos/search `repos`, projects/search `codeReferences`) carry exactly: fullName, url, description, primaryLanguage, stars, lastCommitAt, isArchived, activityState, project, hackathonWinner, scfAwarded, repoScore, repoScoreLabel, tier, kind, stellarEvidence, score, knowledgeNotesCount. Every key is on every row, null where there is no value.

submissions.description: Stored submissions profiled. null when coverage is winners-only: only the winners are on record, so the size of the field is unknown.

rules.description: What the organizer published about submitting and judging. On a DoraHacks event, from its stored event page: absent = the page was not read; a null section = the page has none (on 2026-10-05, 5 of 20 Stellar event pages had a requirements section and 6 a judging section). On an event off DoraHacks (source curated), from its record: the judging sentence it copies from the organizer's page, as judgingCriteria with source and checkedOn, and rubric when the organizer publishes a weighted one; or, when that page was checked and publishes no judging criteria, judgingCriteria null with source, checkedOn and judgingNote. The other keys are absent, not known. Absent on such an event: its organizer's page was not checked (no page on record), which is not a claim that it publishes none.

checkedOn.description: Curated events only: the day that page was checked.

judgingCriteria.description: The page's judging section, in markdown, read from the stored page by the current reader: under the event's own heading that names judging, scoring or criteria (Spanish and Portuguese too), a line of its own or a bold label; sections that sit under different tracks come each under its track's name, and a heading that names both sections serves its criteria part. null = the page was read (readAt) or checked (checkedOn) and has no judging section, as judgingNote says: the organizer published no judging criteria there. It is not an unread page; an unread page has no `rules` at all.

judgingNote.description: Present only when judgingCriteria is null: that the page publishes no judging criteria, with the page and the day it was read or checked. A DoraHacks page's note rests on its sections as read now (a heading, a line of its own or a bold label naming judging, scoring or criteria, in English, Spanish or Portuguese; a list of judges is not criteria).

requirements.description: The page's submission-requirements section, in markdown. null = the page was read (readAt) and has no requirements section: the organizer published none there.

rubric.description: Curated events only: the weighted rubric the organizer publishes, each criterion with its weight in percent in the page's order (not a rank), each scored scoreMin to scoreMax, with the page and day it was checked. Absent: no weighted rubric is on record for this event, which is not a claim that the organizer published none.

byCategory.description: Present only on a slot scored under a different name in each category: one entry per category the event judges in (getHackathon tracks with kind category), with the criterion's name there and what it scores. Absent: the criterion is the same in every category.

scores.description: What the criterion scores, in the page's words.

criterion.description: The page's label for the criterion. A slot the page scores under a different name in each category carries a label that joins the names, as the page writes it; byCategory names each.

weightPercent.description: The criterion's share of the score, in percent; a rubric's weights sum to 100.

scoreMax.description: The highest score a criterion takes. Absent with scoreMin: the page publishes no score scale.

scoreMin.description: The lowest score a criterion takes. Absent with scoreMax: the page publishes no score scale.

source.description: Curated events only: the page the judging sentence, or its absence, was checked against.

stats.description: Counts for the event. totalSubmissions counts the submissions served here (null = no submission list, or only the winners are on record).

coverageNote.description: Present when upstreamSubmissions and totalSubmissions differ: which submissions are not served here (hidden or deleted by their teams, or a same-name resubmission counted once), or that a stored submission DoraHacks no longer lists is kept. When coverage is winners-only: that only the winners are on record, so the size and mix of the field are unknown and the counts of it are null.

hiddenWinners.description: Winning submissions of this event that this page does not serve because their teams hid or deleted them on DoraHacks: each one's placement, award and awardCategory (read as on winners), never the submission itself. placementRank is parsed as served winners' is (placement, else the award's text), so a missing ranked tier joins to it. [] = none; null = no stored DoraHacks roster backs this page, or the read failed.

outcomes.description: Submissions by status after the event, summing to totalSubmissions; null when no submission list is held, or only the winners are (coverage winners-only). Only submissions that are directory projects carry a status; DoraHacks submissions are not classified, so on a DoraHacks event built, inProgress and abandoned are 0 and unknown counts every submission. `profile` says what they became.

totalPrizeUSD.description: Prize money in USD: the event's prize pool, else the sum of its winners' recorded prizes. null = no USD figure is known (a prize not yet announced, or prizes that are not cash); never 0 for unknown.

totalSubmissions.description: The submissions served here. null when no submission list is held, and when coverage is winners-only: only the winners are on record, so the size of the field is unknown, never the winner count.

upstreamSubmissions.description: DoraHacks' own count of the event's submissions (its buidls_count), read daily with the stored event page. null = not a DoraHacks event, or the page has not been read.

winnersNote.description: Why the winners are what they are, so a missing winner or a 0 is explained rather than silent. When hiddenWinners is non-empty: how many winning submissions are not served and why, with each one's placement and award. On an event off DoraHacks: a dated note that its winners are published only in part, or not announced upstream. When winners carry winnerSource: the page that names them and which named winners are not served. On an ended DoraHacks event with no winner served: DoraHacks' winner_announced flag, from its event listing (refreshed hourly), says not announced upstream, or announced but not recorded here. Not announced is never a claim that no one won. null = nothing to add, or the flag could not be read.

tracks.description: The event's tracks: from its submission roster when one is held (on a winners-only event, the tracks of its winners on record); with no roster, the tracks and categories its record declares (kind, description, counts null). [] = the roster names no track. null = not known: no roster and no declared track, or winners that name no track; notes says which.

description.description: Present only on a declared track: one line, in the words of the event's record.

kind.description: Present only on a track the event's record declares (an event with no submission roster): category, a division every entry picks; track, a theme an entry can target.

submissionCount.description: Submissions in the track. null when the event's coverage is winners-only (only its winners are on record, so the track's field is unknown, never its winner count) and on a declared track (no roster held: not known).

totalPrizeUSD.description: Directory rows only: the prize money its winners took.

winnerCount.description: Winners in the track. null on a declared track: no roster held, not known.

submissions.description: Every submission served for the event: [] = a roster read that found none. null = no roster is held (an event off DoraHacks with no curated roster) or none could be read just now (meta.note says which): not checked, never none. On a DoraHacks row `award` and `awardCategory` read as on `winners`: an award its winners of different placements share is `awardCategory`, never a row's `award`.

tracks.description: The event's tracks: from its submission roster when one is held (on a winners-only event, the tracks of its winners on record); with no roster, the tracks and categories its record declares (kind, description, counts null). [] = the roster names no track. null = not known: no roster and no declared track, or winners that name no track; notes says which.

description.description: Present only on a declared track: one line, in the words of the event's record.

kind.description: Present only on a track the event's record declares (an event with no submission roster): category, a division every entry picks; track, a theme an entry can target.

submissionCount.description: Submissions in the track. null when the event's coverage is winners-only (only its winners are on record, so the track's field is unknown, never its winner count) and on a declared track (no roster held: not known).

totalPrizeUSD.description: Directory rows only: the prize money its winners took.

winnerCount.description: Winners in the track. null on a declared track: no roster held, not known.

winners.description: Winner entries. Ordering contract: placementRank is the ONLY per-entry ordering signal; never infer finishing order from array position; check winnersRanked first.

afterEvent.description: What the submitted repo did after the event, in analyzeHackathonSubmissions' activity vocabulary: a commit 90 or more days after the event ended, none by then, archived, or the repo not found. Absent = unknown: the repo's activity was not read, the event has no usable end date (missing or unreadable), or it ended under 90 days ago with no commit past that mark. It describes the submitted repo, not the project: work can move to another repo and a live product can sit still in code, so read `project.status` before calling a build dead.

award.description: This winner's own award as DoraHacks published it: one award per winner ('1st Place - $5,000'), or one prize several winners each won. null = no award named, or an award that names a category (`awardCategory`); what this winner won is then `hackathonPlacement` and `prizeUsd`.

awardCategory.description: The award this winner placed in, when its title names a category or pool, never this winner's prize: this event's winners of other placements share it (a hidden winner's placement counts), or the title states more than this winner's placement. All five Real-World ZK winners share '$10,000 XLM Prize' while placing 1st ($5,000) to 5th ($750); reading it as a winner's prize overstates 3rd place 8 times. null = no other placement of this event is on record under the award and its title states no more than this winner's placement, so the award, if any, reads as the winner's own.

builder.description: Curated roster rows: who built it, as the roster names them; absent when it names no one.

category.description: Directory rows: the project's directory category; null on curated roster rows.

description.description: Project blurb from the submission (markdown stripped).

hackathonPrizeTrack.description: Directory rows: the prize track the project placed in; null when none is recorded, and on curated roster rows. DoraHacks rows carry `track`.

hackathonStatus.description: Directory rows: the project's status after the event (Built, In Progress or Abandoned); null when none is recorded, and on curated roster rows.

id.description: Stable row id (dorahacks-buidl-{id} for live rows, curated-{event}-{name} for a stored submission from an event off DoraHacks, winner-{event}-{name} for a curated roster, from the winner's name).

lastCommitAt.description: The submitted repo's last commit on its default branch when it was last read; null = read, no commit date. Absent = the repo's activity was not read (a repo not found has none to read).

prizeUsd.description: What THIS project won, in USD, parsed from its own placement string ('3rd Place - $1,250 in XLM' -> 1250); on curated roster rows, the roster's own figure. null when the placement carries no amount (tier-labelled winners like 'Track Winner'), never 0, which would assert a prize of nothing.

project.description: The directory project this build became, or null when none is found. Linked when a project lists the build's exact GitHub repo; when none does, when the build's demo site is a project's own website; and when neither, when the build's repo sits under the project's GitHub owner and the build carries the project's name (`basis` says which). The two repo rules also read the repo GitHub now redirects githubUrl to, when the team renamed or transferred it. A winner none of those link can still link when its name is the name of exactly one project and a page says so too: the project's SCF page links this build's DoraHacks page, or the build's DoraHacks page lists the project's website or X account. A shared GitHub owner alone, a name alone, or a shared platform never counts. Absent = not checked (served from a live DoraHacks read), which is not the same as null.

basis.description: repo: the project lists this exact repo. website: the demo site is the project's website. owner-and-name: the repo sits under the project's GitHub owner and the build's name is the project's name, or starts with it. moved-repo: the repo was renamed or transferred (githubUrl redirects on GitHub), and the project lists the repo it moved to. moved-owner-and-name: owner-and-name, read on the repo it moved to. A repo GitHub could not find is never taken as moved. The last two link winners only, when the build's name (a trailing 'Stellar' aside) is the name or an alias of exactly one project: scf-page-and-name: the project's SCF page (scfSourceUrl on searchProjects) links this build's DoraHacks page. submission-links-and-name: this build's DoraHacks page lists the project's website or X account. Absent on links stored before the basis was recorded (all by repo).

factsReadAt.description: When status and scfAwarded were read from the directory (with the submissions index, at most an hour before this response). Absent with them.

scfAwarded.description: Whether SCF funded the project. Absent when it could not be read (unknown).

status.description: The project's directory status today. Absent when it could not be read (unknown).

scfAwarded.description: Curated roster rows: whether the linked directory project has an SCF award on record (scf.awarded); null when the winner links no project on record or that project has no SCF record. Stored DoraHacks winners carry this as project.scfAwarded.

security.description: Present only when this build's repo is held for malware (the repo's own hold is getRepoTrust `security`): the build is still served, but its GitHub link and repo name are withheld (null) and `note` says what not to do, in Scout's words. Absent means no hold on record, which is not a claim that the repo is safe.

shortDescription.description: Curated roster and directory rows: the project's one-line description. DoraHacks rows carry `description` instead.

slug.description: Curated roster rows: the directory project the winner links; null when it links none.

source.description: 'dorahacks' for a DoraHacks submission; 'curated' for a winner stored from a curated record (a curated-{event}-{name} id, an event off DoraHacks). The submissions rows carry the same. Absent on curated roster and directory rows.

url.description: The submission's DoraHacks buidl page; on a curated-{event}-{name} row, the page the win was verified against.

voteCount.description: null on every row since 2026-08: the DoraHacks v1 hub API no longer exposes vote counts. Kept for shape stability; null is unknown, never zero votes.

winnerSource.description: Present only when a page off DoraHacks, not DoraHacks' own winner assignments, names this win: that page, the evidence to cite; the submission's own links stay its DoraHacks ones. The placement is then the place as that page states it, 'Winner' when it names none. Absent on a win DoraHacks assigned, on a submission from an event off DoraHacks (curated-{event}-{name}, whose own link is its source) and on a submission that did not win.

winnersRanked.description: Whether the winners array order is a ranking. true = ordinal placements (sorted by placementRank, winners[0] is 1st place); false = tier-labeled winners (all placementRank null; array order is meaningless, treat as an unordered set); null = no winners recorded.

fallbackChannels.description: Present when the query returns 0 events: a summary plus live announcement channels to point the user at. NOTE: an OBJECT, not an array.

summary.description: What this feed shows for the selected status, naming any other filter (q, organizer, source): not a claim that no Stellar hackathon is upcoming or active elsewhere. When part of the feed could not be read (meta.warnings, partial true), it says so, counts.total is null, and the empty result is not a check.

matchMode.description: How rows matched q: filtered = rows contain the query terms literally; all = no text query (structured filters only).

LeaderboardProject.description: One ranked project row from /api/leaderboard. Every github.* number is as-of meta.dataAsOf (the repo-index rollup timestamp), NOT a live GitHub read; meta.metricDefinitions states what each metric IS.

assetCode.description: Code of the project's issued on-chain asset (USDC, CETES, …), from stellar.expert. Null = no verified issued asset in our on-chain seed set.

assetHolders.description: Trustline holder count of the issued asset. Null when untracked.

assetSupply.description: Circulating supply of the issued asset in whole asset units (sort=supply orders by this). null = NOT TRACKED; never 'zero supply'; untracked issuers sort below every tracked one.

github.description: Rollup across the project's INDEXED repos, as-of meta.dataAsOf.

commits90d.description: Default-branch commits over the trailing 90 days, summed across the project's indexed repos whose scanned code proves Stellar use (stellarProof other than none), from the enrich pass's activitySignals. The sort=activity key. null = no such repo carries a count (an INDEX gap, never zero activity); such rows sort last. This service's own rows are excluded from every ranking; the directory is the instrument, not a subject.

commits90dAsOf.description: The newest activitySignals.asOf among the repos summed into commits90d; the date the count is good for. null when commits90d is null.

lastActivityAt.description: Latest default-branch commit (fallback: last push) across indexed repos. Null when no indexed repo has a known date.

openIssuesTotal.description: Sum of OPEN issues (EXCLUDES pull requests; will not match GitHub's REST open_issues_count). A backlog snapshot, not an activity or quality ranking.

repoCount.description: Indexed repos attributed to the project: our index's coverage, not the project's total GitHub footprint.

repos.description: The exact repositories (owner/name) the stats above aggregate over; repoCount === repos.length, sorted. Lets a consumer reconcile 'activity' against a known set instead of trusting an opaque count; the members are our INDEX's attribution, so a repo absent here may still exist on GitHub (coverage, not a negative claim). Also served in the CSV export as a ';'-joined `repos` column.

totalStars.description: Sum of stargazer counts across indexed repos.

rank.description: 1-based position under THIS response's sort/range/category/type scope; recomputed per request, not a stable global rank. Cite alongside the applied filters (meta.filters).

slug.description: Directory slug: join key to searchProjects for the full profile.

tvlAsOf.description: When tvlUSD was fetched from DefiLlama (dated-metrics rule). Null when untracked.

tvlStale.description: true = tvlAsOf is more than 14 days before this response, or missing, unparseable or in the future. Only the date is checked, not why the figure is old, and sort=tvl still orders by tvlUSD alone, stale or not. false = read within 14 days. null = no tvlUSD.

tvlUSD.description: DefiLlama-verified TVL in USD. null = NOT TRACKED on DefiLlama; never 'zero TVL'; most non-DeFi projects are legitimately untracked. Dated by tvlAsOf.

types.description: Granular product-type tags: the same types[] taxonomy as project-search rows, echoed so a consumer can see WHY a row matched a ?type= filter (#524).

Meta.description: Standard meta block included on every list response

returned.description: Rows in this page (post limit/offset slice)

semantic.description: projects/search only: rows in this page served by the vector-similarity fallback rather than a keyword match (each tagged via:"semantic"; included in `returned` but NOT in `total`). `total` is the keyword match set and is stable across limit AND offset; it used to include these page-one-only rows, so the same query reported total 17 on page one and 6 on page two. On page one `returned` can therefore exceed `total`, and this count is exactly the difference.

total.description: Rows matching the filter before slicing (paginated endpoints). Page until offset + returned >= total. NULL means no honest total exists, never zero and never omitted, and `totalBasis` names why: 'unbounded-similarity-ranking' (searchResearch ranks a bounded candidate pool by similarity, so there is no crisp matching set to count) or 'partial-read' (`partial` is true: a backend read failed, so the matching set could not be counted). Never read a null total as 'no more rows'. Where an endpoint applies no limit, total equals returned and is stated explicitly so a complete read is verifiable rather than inferred.

totalBasis.description: Present only when `total` is null: names why no total exists, 'unbounded-similarity-ranking' or 'partial-read'. Disambiguates the null so it is never read as zero or as a missing field.

failedReads.description: Present wherever `partial` is: the reads that failed on this page, in order; an empty array when `partial` is false. Each names what was read and the failure class only (an error name, a timeout, or the stated reason), never a raw error message.

cause.description: The failure class, e.g. "timeout after 4000ms" or "MongoServerSelectionError".

read.description: What was being read, e.g. "repos search" or "research source=sep".

filters.description: Echo of the filter values this response was computed under (null = filter not applied). Read it to confirm the server saw the filters you sent.

note.description: Optional endpoint-specific reading note: semantics a consumer needs to interpret the rows correctly (counting basis, absence semantics, handoff pointers). Present only where the endpoint has something non-obvious to say.

partial.description: On searchProjects, searchRepos, getBuilders, searchResearch, listSkills and getHackathons, always present: true when at least one backend read failed or timed out and the page went out anyway, so rows may be missing; false when every read completed. A limit or a filter never sets it. Count real loss on this field, not on the 200 status. When a read that feeds the count failed, counts.total is null with totalBasis "partial-read": that page cannot count its matches. A failed read that only decorates served rows (logos, attributions, code evidence) leaves a known total in place.

warnings.description: Present only when there is something to disclose. Two kinds of line share it. (1) A backend read that failed or timed out: the line starts with "backend read failed" and the page may be incomplete; `partial` and `failedReads` carry the same fact as fields. (2) Query parameters this endpoint does not read: names them and states the results are NOT filtered by them. Additive-contract disclosure: the request still succeeds. Two policies, by operation kind, both naming the supported set: the search operations (searchResearch, searchProjects, searchRepos, getPartners, listSkills, getHackathons, getClusters, getLeaderboard, getRfps, getChangelog, getQualityReport, verifyClaim) ignore an unknown parameter and name it here; the registry and lookup operations (listAudits, getChanges, getRwaAssets, getStablecoins, getBuilders, listContracts, searchHackathonBuilds, getPeople, resolveProject, getRepoTrust) reject it with 400 and list the supported parameters in the body (hint, supportedParams or validParams), because a list that looks filtered is worse than a 400.

Partner.description: An ecosystem partner (anchor, ramp, infrastructure, tooling, protocol, wallet, audit firm…). Partner-claimed facts and system-verified signals are SEPARATE fields: `verified` and `trust` are system-computed and cannot be self-reported; everything else is partner/curator-maintained.

assets.description: Asset codes this partner issues/supports, read from their stellar.toml. NULL = no read is recorded (tomlSourceUrl and tomlFetchedAt are not both set), so this is UNKNOWN and never 'issues no assets'; a curated code is never served here. [] = a recorded read declares no CURRENCIES.

caseStudies.description: Curated case studies. NULL = none recorded for this partner (UNKNOWN, never 'has no case studies'); currently null for every partner, as none have been curated yet.

projectSlug.description: Slug in the projects directory, when the case study's project is listed there.

freshness.description: Profile freshness state machine (fresh → aging → stale → archived). Consumers should down-rank or skip partners with excludeFromMatching: true.

pilot.description: Founding pilot-cohort partner (sorts first in unqueried lists).

rampTypes.description: Fiat ramp directions offered (deposit = on-ramp, withdraw = off-ramp). Either confirmed from the anchor's own transfer server /info during a stellar.toml read, or entered by a curator; without a recorded read (tomlSourceUrl and tomlFetchedAt both set) they are curator-entered, so never cite them as stellar.toml facts. NULL = none recorded (UNKNOWN, never 'offers no ramps'), and never inferred from SEP presence.

regions.description: Curated coverage regions. NULL = none recorded for this partner (UNKNOWN, never 'covers nowhere'); the region filter does not select it.

sectors.description: Curated sectors. NULL = none recorded for this partner (UNKNOWN, never 'serves no sector').

seps.description: SEP standards implemented (sep-6, sep-24, sep-31), read from the partner's stellar.toml. NULL = no read is recorded (tomlSourceUrl and tomlFetchedAt are not both set), so we do not know. [] = a recorded read implements none, so [] with non-empty rampTypes is the checkable claim that the ramp is a proprietary API rather than SEP-based. That inference is only valid against [], never against null.

services.description: Curated service tags. NULL = none recorded for this partner (UNKNOWN, never 'offers no services').

tomlConfidence.description: Deterministic trust score for toml-derived anchor facts (basis stellar-toml × freshness of tomlFetchedAt). Null when no read is recorded (tomlSourceUrl and tomlFetchedAt are not both set).

tomlFetchedAt.description: ISO date of the last successful stellar.toml fetch+parse. Admin/partner edits may postdate this snapshot.

tomlSourceUrl.description: The stellar.toml URL the anchor-capability fields (assets/seps/rampTypes/jurisdiction) were last system-enriched from; re-verify there. Null = never toml-enriched (curated/self-reported only).

trust.description: System-computed composite trust (0-1 score + label), decomposed into freshness and verification sub-signals.

label.description: The score's band, computed with it, so not dated either: see score.

score.description: Computed when the row is served from its freshness and verification signals, so not dated itself: the ages of its inputs are freshness.lastPartnerUpdateAt and verified.lastAutoVerifyAt.

url.description: Canonical partner profile page on stellarlight.xyz.

verified.description: SYSTEM-computed activity signals (never self-reported). All-null = not yet auto-verified, NOT a negative signal.

matchMode.description: Present only when q was supplied and rows were returned. scored = ranked by the shared partner scorer over structured capability fields. weak = NOTHING matched q and these are fresh/accepting partners shown as a fallback, NOT matches; treat them as candidates, never as an answer to the query.

matchModeLabel.description: Human-readable statement of the matchMode above, safe to surface verbatim to a user.

validRamps.description: Every value the ramps filter accepts (unknown values 400 with this list).

validRegions.description: Every value the region filter accepts (unknown values 400 with this list). Countries and currencies are not regions; they go in q.

validTypes.description: Every value the type filter accepts (unknown values 400 with this list).

Person.description: One SDF roster entry from /api/people: person, current role, section, and affiliation: quoted from stellar.org/foundation/team with provenance (sourceUrl + observedAt). Roster facts, not verified availability.

observedAt.description: Date this entry was last observed from the source (YYYY-MM-DD).

org.description: Affiliation: 'Stellar Development Foundation' for leadership, the external org for board/advisors, '' when the role names none.

role.description: Current role/title, e.g. 'VP of Ecosystem', 'CEO of Stripe'.

PopulationScope.description: The population a quantitative response aggregated, made answer-visible. Identical `id`s across responses (e.g. analyze vs clusters) mean the numbers are mechanically comparable; different `id`s are DIFFERENT populations; never merge/sum them without labeling the scopes. `truncated: true` means the result is a sample of the population, not a census. Null when the underlying fetch failed.

id.description: Stable digest of collection + filters (NOT count/time), e.g. 'projects|status:Development+Live+Pre-Release'. /api/status sources use 'projects|status:all' (full collection).

included.description: Docs actually aggregated into this response.

statusScope.description: Status filter applied; null = no status filter.

totalAvailable.description: Docs matching the scope in the DB at generation time.

truncated.description: included < totalAvailable: the response is a sample, not the population.

anchorProfile.description: Integration-oriented ramp/anchor profile joined from the partner directory (Anchor-typed rows only; null otherwise). Complements `coverage`: rampTypes says WHAT ramps exist, seps says over WHICH interop surface; `seps: []` with non-empty rampTypes means a proprietary ramp API rather than SEP-6/24, and only against [], never null. NULL SEMANTICS: assets and seps come only from the anchor's stellar.toml and are null unless a read is recorded (the partner's tomlSourceUrl and tomlFetchedAt both set, `profileState: 'profiled'`); rampTypes and regions are as recorded (confirmed from the transfer server or entered by a curator) and null when none is. Null is UNKNOWN, never capability-free. `url` links the full partner profile.

assets.description: From the anchor's stellar.toml. NULL = no read recorded (UNKNOWN); [] = the read found none.

profileState.description: 'profiled' = the anchor's stellar.toml read is recorded, so assets and seps state what it declares; 'not-profiled' = no read is recorded: assets and seps are null (UNKNOWN), and any rampTypes are as a curator entered them.

rampTypes.description: Confirmed from the transfer server or entered by a curator. NULL = none recorded (UNKNOWN).

seps.description: From the anchor's stellar.toml. NULL = no read recorded (UNKNOWN); [] = the read found none.

audits.description: Security-audit rollup from the /api/audits registry (hand-verified projectSlug links): {count, auditors[] (normalized firm names), latestAt (YYYY-MM-DD of the newest report)}. Drift context: driftDays = whole days since the latest report; codeChangedSinceAudit = whether any of the project's joined repos committed on a later day than that report (day-granular; null when either side lacks a date). 'Audited' with high drift is a materially weaker claim; read both. null rollup = no audit on record at our source; NOT a claim the project is unaudited (same absence semantics as /api/audits). Full report rows via /api/audits?project=<slug>; findings text via searchResearch with source=audit.

availability.description: Per-platform availability with as-of dates. null = not curated.

builtBy.description: The organization/entity behind this project ('who built X'), e.g. LOBSTR → Ultra Stellar, Soroswap → Paltalabs. Null when no org is linked. Browse the org's portfolio at https://stellarlight.xyz/entities/{slug}.

canonicalSlug.description: When this record is a known duplicate/rename, the slug of the CANONICAL record to prefer; null for canonical records themselves. Follow it before citing counts or funding.

confidence.description: Blended confidence for this result: overall score (0-1) + label, decomposed into relevance / freshness / authority sub-signals (each 0-1) and ageDays.

coverage.description: Structured corridor/coverage for Anchor-typed projects: answers 'which anchors serve currency/corridor X?' with filterable, dated fields instead of prose. Synced from the matching partner record; null for non-anchors or when no partner record matches.

asOf.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) the coverage was synced from the partner record; cite as the as-of date.

currencies.description: Fiat currencies supported (e.g. MXN, EUR, PHP).

seps.description: Supported SEPs (sep-6, sep-24, sep-31); the on/off-ramp interop surface.

deployment.description: Which network the product is actually deployed on, as a SEPARATE fact from lifecycle status (sls-079: 'Live' used to be read as mainnet-deployed). This is a PROJECT-level fact: mainnet means at least one of the project's products is minted on mainnet, not that every product is; read `products` for per-product state. Populated only from evidence: a verified mainnet contract join, an on-chain activity reading, a minted product in the verified RWA registry (basis rwa-registry, sls-023), or a human-verified operator artifact. A stored network is never overwritten by the registry; only an unknown is filled. network 'unknown' means exactly that: no evidence either way, never 'not deployed'.

basis.description: Evidence class: mainnet-contract-join | onchain-activity | stablecoin-issuance | rwa-registry | human-verified. rwa-registry = a live product in the verified RWA registry (/api/rwa) proves mainnet deployment; sourceUrl is that product's own evidence (the issuer's stellar.toml, or the contract on stellar.expert). Null when network is unknown.

feedbackSignal.description: Aggregated consumer votes for this project (feedback→quality loop): votes = distinct voters (one per hashed IP, latest vote wins), worked = of those, how many voted 'worked'. score = worked/votes, present ONLY once votes pass the anti-gaming floor (≥5 distinct voters); null score with visible counts means 'signal accruing, no ranking influence yet'. Null object = no votes recorded. Aggregated nightly from POST /api/feedback vote kinds.

votes.description: Community votes on the submission, or null; the DoraHacks v1 hub API no longer serves vote counts, and this was previously 0 on every row, asserting that nobody voted rather than that we cannot see votes. An unknown count contributes nothing to build ranking; it neither boosts nor penalises.

identity.description: Rename continuity. Present when this project has former names: aliases resolve to this record in search, and this block carries the provenance. Cite the CURRENT name; mention the alias when the user asked by it.

renamedAt.description: When the current name took effect (if known).

lastActivityAt.description: Most recent commit across the project's own indexed repos; attach as the as-of date for 'is this project active?' answers. Null = no indexed repo with a known commit date (an INDEX gap, e.g. a closed-source product), never 'no activity'.

lifecycle.description: Historical-archive context, present only when a record carries real history (e.g. a defunct project that used to be live); narrate as 'used to be live', not as a current offering. Null for ordinary live records.

links.description: The project OWN canonical homes - cite these as the primary source, not StellarLight or any directory. Only present, non-empty fields are included.

llamaSlugs.description: The curated DefiLlama protocol slugs whose rows SUM to tvlUSD (several per project, e.g. Blend = pools + backstops). The mapped-provider identifiers tvlMethod refers to: follow each as https://defillama.com/protocol/{slug} for the provider's own page and full TVL time series (history/peak/record live at the provider; this API serves the current dated point only). Null = not llama-mapped (matches tvlUSD null = not tracked).

networksBasis.description: What evidence stands behind supportedNetworks, and therefore whether the list is exhaustive. 'curated' = curator-maintained from the project's own docs; the list is intended to be complete, so an absent chain is informative. The rest are DERIVED proofs that the project operates on Stellar, strongest first: 'onchain-activity' (contract records observed on Stellar), 'defillama-tvl' (DefiLlama tracks its Stellar TVL), 'anchor-coverage' (SEP/corridor rails), 'scf-award' (the Stellar Community Fund funds only Stellar work). A derived basis yields exactly ['stellar'] and is NOT exhaustive; other chains are unknown, not excluded. NULL = no basis, which pairs with a null supportedNetworks.

onchain.description: On-chain metrics from stellar.expert for hand-verified contract/asset join keys. null = not tracked in our registry. NEVER 'no on-chain activity'. contracts[]: {address, label, events, subinvocations, storageEntries, createdAt, verifiedRepo}; events and subinvocations are LIFETIME counts (a contract users call directly at top level can show low subinvocations despite heavy use; read events alongside). Asset-issuer activity: assetHolders = accounts holding a balance TODAY (the active-address count); assetTrustlines = accounts that have EVER opened a trustline (reach, always >= assetHolders; do NOT read it as the active count); assetPayments = lifetime count of payment operations (the transaction-volume metric); assetTrades = lifetime trade count; assetPaymentsAmount = lifetime payment volume in WHOLE ASSET UNITS, not USD (a same-denomination count, not comparable across assets without a price); assetSupply = whole asset units. From the second weekly snapshot, delta fields activate: per-contract eventsDelta/subinvocationsDelta, assetHoldersDelta, assetPaymentsDelta, with prevAsOf + deltaDays defining the window; null deltas mean no prior snapshot yet, NOT zero activity. source + asOf date every payload.

onchainContractsCount.description: view=compact rows only: how many entries the left-out `onchain.contracts` list has. Null = no on-chain record was read for this project, not zero contracts. Absent on full rows, which carry `onchain` itself.

placementRank.description: Numeric rank parsed from hackathonPlacement (1 = best), handling both digit ('1st Place') and word ('First Place') ordinals, or null when the source gives no ordinal (a flat 'Winners' bucket). winners[] is sorted by placementRank, so winners[0] is the 1st-place entry when the event has ranked placements; unranked winners (placementRank: null) sort last and their order is not significant. Sort/filter on placementRank instead of parsing the label.

productKind.description: Curated product-kind for wallet-class records (hardware-wallet | mobile-app | browser-extension | web-app | protocol | sdk-kit). null = not-yet-classified (never a negative claim).

products.description: Per-PRODUCT deployment records (#742): provider status and product-on-network status are DIFFERENT statements. A Live project row NEVER establishes that a given product is live on a given network; read this array for that, and if it is null you do not have the answer and must go to the operator. Curated only; every record carries evidenceUrl + asOf so the claim is re-verifiable at its source. NULL = no product-level records modelled for this project (UNKNOWN, never 'this project ships no products'). Fed by the verified RWA registry (/api/rwa; every row dated by its own verifiedAt) for the issuers that have a project row: WisdomTree, Spiko, Etherfuse, Ondo, Figure, Circle, Paxos, Centrifuge and others, plus hand-curated rows. Only MINTED registry rows are served here (registryState live or issued-single-holder); an asset the issuer declares or deployed with zero supply is tracked in the registry but is not a product. WHETHER THIS LIST IS COMPLETE for the issuer is a separate fact: read the sibling `productsCoverage`; declared / tracked / served against the issuer's own declaration (its stellar.toml, or its deployer's contract history), `complete` only when every declared asset is tracked and every issuer account was reconciled, null when that cannot be stated. Still null on most projects. kind: oracle-feed | rwa-asset | stablecoin | wallet-app | bridge | ramp | other; network: mainnet | testnet | futurenet; status: live | development | announced | retired.

assetId.description: CODE-GISSUER for a classic asset, the contract id for a Soroban token; the product's identity.

controls.description: Issuer flags from Horizon for a classic asset: authRequired (whitelist), authRevocable (freeze), clawbackEnabled, authImmutable. null on Soroban tokens and hand-curated rows.

issuer.description: The issuer label the RWA registry carries for the product (getRwaAssets issuerEntity: the rwa.xyz listing's name, a brand, product line or fund as often as a legal entity), not read from the issuer's stellar.toml. Null on hand-curated rows.

launchedAt.description: Contract creation date (Soroban); null for classic assets, which Horizon does not date.

registryState.description: The registry's own state: live | issued-single-holder, since `status` (the stored enum) cannot say 'minted but held only by the issuer'.

tomlStatus.description: The issuer toml's own `status` for the asset where it was read (live | private | test …); null = not read. `private` = a restricted offering (minted and held, not a public market) and `note` says so. Hand-curated records: null.

verificationLevel.description: How the registry verified this product (see getRwaAssets methodology); null on hand-curated rows.

productsCoverage.description: Whether `products` is COMPLETE for the issuer accounts this project joins (sls-083). The comparison set is what those accounts' own stellar.toml declared on asOf (the RWA registry's issuer coverage table): declared = (code, issuer) pairs the tomls declare under the covered accounts; tracked = of those, registry rows in any state; complete = declared === tracked AND issuersUnreconciled === 0; a project with an issuer whose toml could not be read is never 'complete' (Circle: false). served = REGISTRY-fed product records on this row (minted states only, one per paired tranche; `products` may also carry hand-curated records); it is a different count from tracked: it can be smaller (a zero-supply asset is tracked but not a product) or larger (the registry tracks an issued asset the toml omits, verificationLevel on-chain-home-domain). NULL = completeness cannot be stated: no joined issuer has a toml to reconcile and no deployer entry exists (on-chain-only classic issuers, hand-curated products); null is never 'complete'. issuersUnreconciled counts the issuer accounts the statement does NOT cover: classic issuers whose toml could not be read, plus one for the project's Soroban tokens when it has any (they have no toml).

basis.description: issuer-stellar-toml = classic assets, compared against what the issuer accounts' own stellar.toml declares. deployer-contracts = Soroban tokens (no toml), compared against every SEP-41 token contract the deployer account behind this project's tokens has created, read from Horizon's create-contract history; the issuer's own act, and wider than rwa.xyz's listing (Spiko: 17 token contracts deployed, 9 listed, 8 with zero supply tracked as deployed-no-supply). A deployer can be a platform creating tokens for several issuers (Centrifuge deploys for Anemoy too), so declared counts the deployer's tokens the registry attributes to this project plus any it has attributed to nobody; test and superseded contracts are excluded with a recorded reason, and a token that is neither a row nor excluded makes complete false for every client of that deployer.

prominence.description: Editorial ranking boost (0-100); higher = more canonical for its category.

publicGoods.description: SCF Public Goods Award recipient data: {awardRounds[] (e.g. 2025Q4: CSV-confirmed rounds only, requested-amount tranches with Status=Awarded, not payout proof), evidenceUrl}. null = not a confirmed recipient at our source. NEVER 'not a public good'. Q2'26 outcomes live on Tansu and are excluded until readable.

repos.description: This project’s top indexed GitHub repos, surfaced inline (same shape as /api/repos/search items). Cite as the project’s code references.

reposCount.description: view=compact rows only: how many entries the left-out `repos` list has (0 = that list is empty on the full row). Null = not known. Absent on full rows, which carry `repos` itself.

routes.description: Curated ROUTE-LEVEL bridge evidence for Bridge-typed records. A project hit alone is DISCOVERY-only: it never establishes that a specific transfer route exists, which direction is supported, or what the destination asset representation is (canonical Circle-issued USDC vs a bridged representation like USDC.axl). Each row here is a curator-verified route fact grounded in the provider's own docs (sourceUrl + asOf). Null = no curated route evidence (UNKNOWN, never 'no routes exist'). Quote-time facts (fees, live availability, current quotes) are intentionally NOT encoded; confirm those with the provider at transfer time.

asOf.description: YYYY-MM-DD the route evidence was verified; routes are dated facts, re-verify before relying on them for a live transfer.

assetRepresentation.description: What the DESTINATION asset is: 'canonical' = issuer-native (e.g. Circle-issued USDC via CCTP burn-mint), 'wrapped'/'bridged'/'interchain' = a representation (e.g. USDC.axl). Null = quote-time/unverified; never assume canonical.

assets.description: Asset codes moved on this route (e.g. USDC). Empty = asset scope not curated (unknown, not none).

direction.description: 'bidirectional' = the reverse leg is also evidenced; 'one-way' = only fromChain→toChain is. Null = direction not verified.

fromChain.description: Source network, lowercase: same vocabulary as supportedNetworks ('evm' is the EVM umbrella).

sourceUrl.description: Provider source the route evidence was verified from.

scfAmountStatus.description: Disambiguates a null award amount: 'undisclosed' = the SCF award is confirmed but no amount is published in the source data (NOT a data gap; do not guess); 'disclosed' = scfTotalAwardedUSD carries the number; null = not awarded.

scfAsOf.description: ISO date the SCF award facts were last verified against the source. Pair with scfSourceUrl to re-verify a stored claim.

scfAwardedRounds.description: SCF round numbers this project was awarded in (e.g. [2, 17, 22]), from official award pages. Rounds are authoritative. EMPTY IS NOT 'NO SCF FUNDING': SCF grants awards outside the numbered rounds (a Liquidity Award carries no SCF #N), so a project can hold real award money with this array empty; check scfTotalAwardedUSD and read scfRoundAwards, where such awards appear with round null and their own awardName. Per-award official amounts live in scfRoundAwards; scfTotalAwardedUSD is the project's SCF-page total and can exceed their sum (top-ups SCF doesn't itemize per round).

scfBasis.description: Evidence class behind the SCF award facts: 'official-record' = parsed from the communityfund.stellar.org submission cards; 'human-verified' = curated correction where the official page is ambiguous. Null = provenance not yet stamped (legacy rows; populates as enrichment re-reaches them).

scfConfidence.description: Deterministic trust score for the SCF award facts: basis-class weight × stepwise freshness decay. score 0-1, label high/medium/low, ageDays since last verification. Null = no recorded provenance (absence of evidence, never a low score). Same provenance ⇒ same score: cacheable.

scfRoundAwards.description: The official submission record per AWARD: the reconciling basis for scfTotalAwardedUSD. Each entry: the round number (null for an award SCF does not number), the award's own name (present only on those), the published submission budget in USD (null = award confirmed, budget not published; never guessed), and the official award type (e.g. 'Legacy v5.0 Community Award'). Not every SCF award belongs to a numbered round: a Liquidity Award carries no SCF #N, so a project can hold real award money while scfAwardedRounds is empty; read this array before treating an empty scfAwardedRounds as 'no SCF funding'. scfAwardedRounds stays numeric-only by design. The page-level total can legitimately exceed the sum of these budgets; treat these as the per-award truth and the total as SCF's own aggregate.

scfSourceUrl.description: Official SCF project page the award facts were read from; the citation for scfAwardedRounds/scfRoundAwards/scfTotalAwardedUSD.

score.description: Relevance score for the current query (higher = better match)

status.description: Lifecycle status of the PROJECT, never a deployment claim (sls-079). 'Live' means the product is operating for users somewhere; it does NOT assert Stellar mainnet deployment; read the sibling `deployment` field for that fact. 'Pre-Release' includes testnet-only products. 'Inactive' = defunct/archived; such projects stay name-searchable but are heavily down-ranked and excluded from the leaderboard/directory. statusAsOf/statusSourceUrl/statusBasis carry the label's provenance.

statusAsOf.description: When the current status value was last asserted/verified (ISO 8601). Null = undated legacy label: treat the status as source-relative, not freshly confirmed.

statusBasis.description: What kind of evidence backs the current status, WEAKEST LAST: 'human-verified' = a curator confirmed it, 'onchain-activity' = a contract/network probe, 'repo-activity' = the project's OWN indexed repository committed inside a dated window, which for a LIBRARY or SDK is what liveness means (it is deliberately not awarded to deployed products, where a commit shows the team is working but not that the service runs), 'package-release' = a versioned artifact shipped to a package registry (npm, jsr.io) whose own metadata names this project's repository as its source, published inside a dated window; publication evidence for a library, never proof anything is deployed, 'product-integration' = the LIVE product itself was found to reference Stellar infrastructure (a SEP-1 stellar.toml, a Horizon/Soroban RPC endpoint, an on-chain address, or a Stellar SDK in its own bundle); an integration OBSERVED on the deployed surface, stronger than a page merely answering but NEVER a claim the product works or that a human looked, 'site-liveness' = the product surface was reachable when checked (reachable is not maintained; a parked domain and a dead product's marketing site both pass it), 'operator-announcement' = the team said so, and it can describe PLANS rather than deployment; read statusAsOf and the description. The last two are ADMISSIONS, not evidence: 'source-inherited' means the label was carried over from the upstream ecosystem database and NOBODY HAS INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED IT; it is the default and currently the majority of rows; 'unverified' means the same with no citable source. A Live label on either basis is a record of what a seed list said, never proof the project is running or that anything is deployed on mainnet. Null = provenance not recorded. statusAsOf dates the OBSERVATION behind the basis, not the last sync.

statusCaveat.description: Present only with statusChecks. On a Live row with a hit, one sentence to relay with the status: the label may describe a product that stopped or moved (a protocol deprecated upstream can have a successor), so treat Live as unconfirmed. A check never changes the status itself. Null = no check hit, or the row is not Live; read statusChecks for what was checked.

statusChecks.description: Checks of the status label against stored upstream facts, present only on rows with a DefiLlama link (llamaSlugs); absent means the row has no DefiLlama link, so neither check applies. defillama-listing: hit when DefiLlama marks every linked slug dead (a deadFrom date, or deprecated with nothing locked and no live listing in its parentProtocol family), clear when it lists one as active, could-not-check when it was not read yet, a slug is missing upstream (a rename or removal), or a deprecated slug looks superseded (no deadFrom while value is still locked or a family listing is live): deprecated alone is never a hit. tvl-zero-onchain-quiet, only for DEX, Lending, Bridge and Yield rows: hit when a DefiLlama TVL of 0 read within the last 14 days, over a listing that found every linked slug, meets 60 or more days of observed time in which no tracked contract emitted an event or took a sub-call (both counters read for every contract), clear when a fresh TVL is above 0 or a contract moved in the latest window, could-not-check otherwise (no TVL figure or one that is negative, a TVL reading older than 14 days, a listing with a linked slug missing upstream, no tracked contract, a counter not read, a reading date that cannot be read, or under 60 days observed). A could-not-check result is not a clean bill.

asOf.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the reading the result rests on; null when there was none.

detail.description: What was read, or why it could not be read, in plain words with dates.

sourceUrl.description: Where to check the fact: the first linked protocol's DefiLlama page (its listing and TVL figure); the contract readings behind the TVL check are the row's onchain block.

statusConfidence.description: Deterministic trust score for the lifecycle status fact: basis-class weight times stepwise freshness decay. score 0 to 1, label high/medium/low, ageDays since last verification. Null = no recorded provenance (absence of evidence, never a low score). The same provenance gives the same score, so it can be cached. Halved on a Live row when a statusChecks entry is a hit (statusCaveat says why).

statusSourceUrl.description: Primary evidence URL behind the current status (operator announcement, checked product surface, on-chain probe). Null on legacy rows.

supportedNetworks.description: Blockchain networks this project supports, lowercase (e.g. ['stellar','xrpl']). READ THIS WITH networksBasis. Only when networksBasis is 'curated' is the array intended to be COMPLETE; that is the case where a missing chain is meaningful. For every other basis the array is DERIVED from evidence that the project operates on Stellar, lists only ['stellar'], and says NOTHING about any other chain: a derived row is not a claim of Stellar-only. NULL = we hold neither curation nor evidence (UNKNOWN, never 'supports no networks'). To establish that a project does NOT support a chain you need a source, not this field.

tvlAsOf.description: When tvlUSD was fetched from DefiLlama (ISO 8601).

tvlMethod.description: How tvlUSD was computed (e.g. sum of the mapped DefiLlama protocol rows in llamaSlugs, USD at DefiLlama pricing time): the inclusion-scope note that lets a consumer reconcile modest cross-source differences instead of calling them contradictions.

tvlMethodUrl.description: Citation URL for the project's PRIMARY mapped DefiLlama protocol row (first of llamaSlugs): the provider/method page to cite alongside tvlUSD. When llamaSlugs has multiple entries, tvlUSD sums ALL of them, so this page shows one component, not necessarily the whole sum; enumerate llamaSlugs for the full inclusion set. Null when not llama-mapped.

tvlSource.description: Source that produced tvlUSD (e.g. 'defillama'). Null = legacy value predating provenance. Concurrent sources (operator site, DefiLlama, Dune) legitimately differ by pricing time and inclusion scope; cite tvlUSD as '<tvlSource> as of <tvlAsOf>', never as exact universal truth.

tvlStale.description: true = tvlAsOf is more than 14 days before this response, or missing, unparseable or in the future: cite tvlUSD with its tvlAsOf as a past reading, not today's TVL. Only the date is checked, not why the figure is old. false = read within 14 days. null = no tvlUSD.

tvlUSD.description: Total value locked in USD per DefiLlama, summed across the protocol's tracked components. null = NOT TRACKED on DefiLlama (never 'zero TVL'); with llamaSlugs set, null means the linked DefiLlama protocol publishes no TVL figure for Stellar (an aggregator, or a protocol DefiLlama stopped computing). Refreshed weekly; see tvlAsOf, and tvlStale for a reading more than 14 days old.

types.description: Capability tags (Wallet, DEX, Lending, Oracle, SDK, RPC, Faucet, NFT, RWA, Anchor, Stablecoin, Indexer, Explorer, Security, Gaming).

venueRole.description: Role in the DEX/trading landscape. 'amm' and 'native-orderbook' are INDEPENDENT LIQUIDITY VENUES; 'aggregator-router' routes across venues and runs none; 'trading-ui' is an interface over other venues (e.g. the native SDEX); 'wallet-integrated' is trading embedded in a wallet. A DEX type/cluster count is a directory TAXONOMY count, not a competitor or venue count; count venueRole in ('amm','native-orderbook') for independent venues. Null = not yet classified (unknown, NOT 'not a venue').

via.description: How this result was matched: keyword (token or synonym overlap) or semantic (vector-similarity fallback, a guess to verify, not a match). Null only on a view=compact row whose full row had no via.

codeReferences.description: Top graded repos matching the same query, surfaced inline (max 5, first page only; same shape as /api/repos/search). Cite as existing code references for prior-art questions.

advisory.description: Present when the page does NOT contain a keyword match for the query; either nothing was found at all, or `matchMode` is `semantic`, meaning every row is a vector neighbour rather than a match. In the semantic case the rows are still returned (a neighbour is occasionally the right answer for a conceptual query) but they must NOT be reported as the thing asked for: a query for a project name that lands here means we hold no project by that name. `suggestions[]` carries the endpoints that can still answer it (repo search for code-only entities, the research corpus for prose mentions).

anchorProfileBasis.description: Present only when the page carries anchor rows: null semantics for the anchorProfile join. assets and seps are null without a recorded stellar.toml read (see each profile's profileState), rampTypes and regions null when none is recorded; a null is never a negative capability claim.

didYouMean.description: Present when the query as typed matched NOTHING and a fuzzy name lookup recovered exactly one project within a typo's distance: the results are for `to`, not for what was asked, and `matchMode` is `corrected`. Only fires for short (≤2 token) queries against names of 5+ characters, and only when a single candidate wins outright, so it never guesses between similar names and never touches 3 to 4 character asset tickers. Relay the correction to the user rather than presenting the rows as a match for the original spelling.

from.description: The query as the caller typed it.

matchMode.description: Tier of match relaxation that produced these results. `semantic` means NO keyword tier matched: every row is a vector-similarity fallback guess (each tagged `via: "semantic"`, confidence capped at medium), so verify relevance before relying on them. `corrected` means the rows matched only through a spelling correction, either a known one (e.g. strupey to stroopy) or a typo-distance name recovery reported in `didYouMean` (e.g. frieghter to Freighter): the query token does not occur in them, so verify the identity before treating them as evidence about the queried name.

scfCountBasis.description: Counting basis for the SCF fields on rows: scfTotalAwardedUSD is the project's own SCF-page total (SDF's figure); scfRoundAwards carries each awarded round's official submission record, and the total can exceed the sum of round budgets (un-itemized top-ups).

semantic.description: True when the keyword pass was thin and vector-similarity rows filled the page (each such row tagged via:'semantic'). Distinct from matchMode='semantic', which means NO keyword tier matched at all.

Repo.description: An indexed Stellar ecosystem GitHub repository graded by repoScore. Cite the repo's url / homepageUrl as the primary source.

activitySignals.description: Velocity + release snapshot captured by the enrich pass, dated by asOf. Null = not yet captured for this repo (rows backfill on the weekly refresh), never zero-activity. commits90d counts default-branch commits in the 90 days before asOf; the velocity discriminator WITHIN activityState (two 'active' repos can differ 50x here).

activityState.description: Observable activity state derived at serve time from lastCommitAt + isArchived: active = commit ≤45d; maintained = ≤180d; dormant = a KNOWN commit older than 180d (an observation; dormant repos can be complete, not dead); archived = the owner's own declaration (the only death verdict); unknown = no commit date held; never read unknown or dormant as defunct.

canonical.description: True when surfaced as a curated canonical answer for an infra, protocol or developer-product query (e.g. error codes → stellar-core and the SDKs; Horizon → stellar/stellar-horizon; Scaffold Stellar → stellar-scaffold/cli; Stellar Lab → stellar/laboratory; smart contract examples → stellar/soroban-examples). Floated to the top; meta.canonical lists them. A query that is a full owner/name path fires no canonical entry and ranks the repo it names first; a bare name that fires one ranks the canonical repo first and repos with that exact name next (q=sep-10: stellar/stellar-protocol, then a repo named sep10); a bare name that fires none ranks the repo with that exact name first.

ciPresent.description: CI config present in-tree (.github/workflows, CircleCI, GitLab CI) per the latest code scan. Presence only. NOT a claim CI passes. null = not yet scanned for this fact.

codeInUse.description: Mainnet usage rollup for contracts attributed to this repo (scanner-verified contract ids + stellar.expert wasm validation; refreshed weekly): contracts = attributed contract count; events/subinvocations = LIFETIME counts summed across them; eventsDelta/subinvocationsDelta = change since the prior weekly snapshot (null until one exists; NOT zero activity). null object = no verified mainnet contract joined to this repo: absence of a join, never a claim the code is unused. The dynamic half of code truth: codeDepth says the code is serious, codeInUse says it is LIVE.

codeVerified.description: Code-verified truth from analyzing the repo's ACTUAL source (not stars/topics): the discriminator between 'popular' and 'real, current, deep Soroban code'. Null until the repo has been code-scanned. Use to qualify an answer: prefer a deployable contract on a supported soroban-sdk over tooling that merely uses Stellar.
