codeConfidence.description: Deterministic trust score for the code facts (basis code-scan × freshness of scannedAt). Null when never scanned.

codeDepth.description: 0-1 substance of the actual contract code (auth/storage/arith/branch, not mere presence). ~0.6+ = a real, non-trivial contract; low = scaffold/template. Null for non-Rust proofs.

codeDomains.description: Evidence-only domain labels derived at scan time from ecosystem dependencies + capability tags + contract-interface traits; what the CODE proves the repo does, never README self-description: defi-lending, defi-amm, defi-yield, oracle, payments-x402, wallet-infra, anchor-ramp, indexer. [] = nothing domain-specific proven (an honest null).

contractInterface.description: Soroban contract ABI: full pub fn signatures per #[contractimpl] block, formatted `Contract.fn(arg: Type, …) -> Ret` (host-injected env param stripped, matching the SDK contractspec). Symbols say WHAT a repo implements; this says HOW TO CALL IT. Empty for non-contract repos or repos scanned before 2026-08-08.

contractInterfacePaths.description: The repo-relative source file of each contractInterface entry, same order and length: contractInterfacePaths[i] is where contractInterface[i] is defined at scannedRef. Interfaces in test code (tests/, __tests__/, fixtures/, testdata/, e2e/, fuzz targets, test helpers, suites and contracts, test wasm workspaces, test files such as foo_test.rs, and test contracts inside an integration/ folder) are left out of contractInterface; one under an examples or template folder is kept, and its path says so. Only contractInterface, symbols and sdkCapabilities leave test code out; stellarProof, codeDepth, isDeployableContract and stellarDeps still read every fetched file until a measured follow-up, so a repo whose only Soroban crate is a test fixture can serve an empty contractInterface beside a cargo-sdk proof. [] when the scan that recorded paths found no interface. null when no paths were recorded: the repo was scanned before 2026-11-04, and such a scan also read integration-test, testdata, e2e and test wasm folders, so an entry may be a test fixture until the next scan.

isDeployableContract.description: This repo's PRODUCT is a deployable Soroban contract (Cargo cdylib; vs a CLI/indexer/frontend that only uses Stellar). Known platform/SDK/tooling repos (stellar-core, rs-soroban-env, the SDKs/CLI/RPC…) are pinned FALSE even though they vendor cdylib crates; those are runtime/fixtures, not a deployable contract product.

mainnetContractId.description: README-claimed contract id VERIFIED to exist on Stellar mainnet at scan time (stellar.expert echo-check): unfakeable deployment evidence. Null when no verified address.

protocolCaps.description: CAPs (Core Advancement Proposals) whose declared protocolVersion matches targetProtocol: the protocol-change grounding for this repo's SDK line, joined from the committed cap-registry. Answers 'which consensus/protocol changes are relevant to this contract's SDK pin'. Empty when targetProtocol is null.

scannedAt.description: When the code was last scanned.

scannedRef.description: Commit SHA the facts were computed at; cite github.com/<fullName>/tree/<scannedRef>. Null on scans before 2026-08-12.

sdkCapabilities.description: Stellar SDK capability tags detected in the repo's JS/TS sources; what a dapp actually DOES with the SDK: tx-building, signing, x402/mpp agent payments, soroban-rpc, contract-invoke, horizon, sep10-auth, sep24-ramp, wallet-kit, passkey, fee-bump. Closed tag set; [] = no JS sources analyzed yet or none detected (scan-dated, not a negative).

sorobanSdkVersion.description: Raw soroban-sdk version requirement (a sourced fact; never a bare protocol integer).

stellarDeps.description: Stellar-ecosystem dependencies from the repo's manifests (Cargo.toml dependency sections + package.json dep maps), allowlist-matched package names stored verbatim: the dependency graph. Forward read: the repo's stack. Reverse read: search the package name to find dependents (adoption evidence no README mention can fake). Empty until a post-2026-08-10 scan.

stellarProof.description: How we verified it's Stellar, strongest→weakest: cargo-sdk (soroban-sdk dep) / contract-macros (#[contract] usage) / lang-sdk (Swift/Kotlin/Go/Python Stellar SDK) / js-sdk / stellar-toml. 'none' = the repo WAS scanned and no direct Stellar code evidence was found (a scanned general-purpose dependency); such repos rank below Stellar-evidenced ones and carry stellarEvidence 'none' unless their own text mentions Stellar.

symbols.description: Public code-symbol surface (pub fn/struct/enum/trait names) extracted from the scanned Rust sources: what the repo IMPLEMENTS (e.g. release_escrow, swap_exact_tokens). Also a search signal: queries match these. Empty for repos scanned before 2026-07-08 or non-Rust proofs.

targetProtocol.description: Stellar protocol the pinned soroban-sdk MAJOR targets, derived from the maintained sdk→protocol table (dated; the mapping has documented irregularities: 23.x spans P24→P25). ADVISORY, not an attestation: null = unknown major, never guessed.

versionStatus.description: soroban-sdk status vs the latest protocol at scan time. 'unknown' (rc/git/unpinned) never implies staleness.

deepWikiUrl.description: DeepWiki AI-generated wiki of this repo's internals (deepwiki.com/{owner}/{name}). Hand off here for deep 'where/how' code questions (e.g. where error codes / consensus / XDR are defined) beyond which-repo discovery.

deprecatedAt.description: The date the repo ITSELF gives for its archive or deprecation (YYYY-MM-DD): GitHub's archive banner, a release notice. null when the repo gives none; never the date we read it.

kind.description: What KIND of repo this is, DERIVED at read time from the row's own stored signals (nothing new is stored or researched), first match wins: isArchived → archived; isFork → fork; a curated Stellar platform repo (protocol, network services such as Horizon and RPC, SDKs, CLI) → platform; a template/example/tutorial-looking name → template-or-tutorial; codeVerified.isDeployableContract → contract; linked to a directory product (project) → application; judgedHackathon → hackathon (a judged entry that is neither a contract nor a listed product; one that became a product is an application: the product link outranks where the code was first submitted); else code; a hackathon demo, a fork and a shipped product are not equal references, so weigh it by kindBasis.

kindBasis.description: The signal that decided kind, so the label can be weighed: isArchived | isFork | knownPlatform (the curated Stellar platform registry) | judgedHackathon | nameLooksTemplate (the one heuristic: a name pattern such as '*-template', 'hello-world', 'example', 'tutorial'; the rest are stored facts) | isDeployableContract | projectSlug | none (fell through to code).

knowledgeNotes.description: Dated FACTS about this repo with named sources: curated (hand-verified: packaging, doc maps, companion repos) or derived:audit (the owning project has verified security-audit reports in the registry; exact projectSlug join). Never summaries, never guesses; empty when nothing is on record.

knowledgeNotesCount.description: view=compact rows only: how many entries the left-out `knowledgeNotes` list has (0 = none on record). Null = not known. Absent on full rows, which carry `knowledgeNotes` itself.

project.description: The curated project this repo is linked to, if any.

renamedFrom.description: The renamed path the request named, when the index holds no row for it and this repo, where GitHub redirects it, stands in for it on searchRepos (issue #1901: the Stellar docs link github.com/theahaco/scaffold-stellar, now stellar-scaffold/cli). null when the repo was found under the name asked for.

repoScore.description: Quality grade (0-100) = freshness + traction + hackathon/SCF/builder authority. Lead with high-score repos.

score.description: Keyword-relevance score for the current query (higher = better match).

source.description: Discovery provenance: project-link = from the curated directory's github links; ec-taxonomy = from Electric Capital's public crypto-ecosystems list.

stellarEvidence.description: WHY this repo ranks as Stellar-relevant: ranking puts Stellar evidence ABOVE raw keyword score, and this names the tier: code-verified (scan found real Stellar/Soroban code) / sdf-org / curated (canonical or flagship map) / mentioned (stellar|soroban in its own name/topics/description/README) / none: a general-purpose toolchain or dependency with NO direct Stellar evidence. 'none' rows can still topic-match a query (e.g. a ZK language for q=zero-knowledge): treat them as toolchains, never cite them as Stellar reference implementations.

successorRepo.description: Analog: this repo is a SUPERSEDED generation and the named fullName is its successor (curated, verified against the repos' own statements, never inferred from names). Null = not superseded or not yet classified. In searchRepos, when the successor (this field, else supersededBy) is also in the results, the successor takes this repo's place and this repo moves below it, unless q is an exact alias of this repo's owner, name or path.

supersededBy.description: Where to go instead, as GitHub spells it; from the curated dated supersession map (P5), falling back to the stored successorRepo. null = no curated supersession statement for this repo, never 'not superseded'.

supersessionKind.description: archived = GitHub archived the repo; renamed = the path 301s to a new one; deprecated = the package or repo carries a deprecation notice; superseded = a newer generation exists and the repo says so.

testsPresent.description: Test files/dirs present in-tree (tests/, __tests__, *.test.*, *_test.*) per the latest code scan. Presence only. NOT a coverage or quality claim. null = not yet scanned for this fact.

tier.description: Quality tier (tag-and-demote): quality = high-grade, community = alive but unproven, archive = GitHub-archived or dead-and-unstarred; demoted in ranking and excluded from inline code references, but never deleted (name lookups still find it). Lead with quality-tier repos.

tierChangedAt.description: When the tier last changed: the date that covers `tier` and `tierReason`. Null when the lane has never judged the row; do not date the tier from scannedAt or lastCommitAt, which describe the scan and the repo.

tierReason.description: WHY the tier is what it is: the enum reasons the code-tier lane recorded when it last judged this row (e.g. curated-canonical, or the archive keys). Null until that lane has judged the row: a bare tier with no reason means the value is the schema default, not a verdict.

canonical.description: The curated canonical repos floated to the top for an infra, protocol or developer-product query (e.g. error codes → stellar/stellar-core; Scaffold Stellar → stellar-scaffold/cli), the same on every page: the query's canonical repos the index holds, whether or not this page or a filter serves them. null when the query isn’t a canonical-routed concept.

eligible.description: Rows the request's filters admit in the index. Equals total when truncated is false. When truncated is true: the database's count for a browse with no q whose filters all run there (language, minScore), and null for a search or an activity, capability, domain or dependsOn filter, where only ranking every row could count the matches. Never read null as zero.

truncated.description: True when the ranking was cut at its candidate window: the top 200 rows by repoScore for a browse with no q, the top 600 for a search or a capability, domain or dependsOn filter. Rows past the window were never ranked, so total counts the window and paging ends at it; read eligible for the number of matching rows. False when the ranking holds every row the filters admit.

matchMode.description: How well this page matched the query, judged by its best row. strict = the best row matched every query term (other rows may match fewer; counts.total counts every row that matched at least one term, plus curated canonical and flagship repos and exact owner or name matches); partial = the best row matched some terms; corrected = the best rows matched only through a known spelling correction (e.g. strupey → stroopy), so the query token does not occur in them: verify the identity before treating them as evidence about the queried name; weak = NONE did and the rows are ranked neighbours, not matches; all = no query supplied; none = the search failed (NOT evidence of absence). Treat corrected/weak/none rows as candidates requiring verification, never as findings.

matchModeLabel.description: Human-readable statement of the matchMode above, safe to surface verbatim to a user.

note.description: How to read the results (e.g. code references graded by repoScore 0-100).

RequestError.description: The request itself was wrong (a 400): fix the call, do not retry it as is.

ResearchResult.description: One ranked research chunk from /api/research (best chunk per document).

capProtocolVersion.description: source=cap only: the protocol version this CAP shipped in, from its own preamble. Null = not declared upstream (drafts/TBD); never guessed. The join key between protocol history and soroban-sdk versions.

capStatus.description: source=cap only: the CAP's own declared Status from its preamble (Final, Implemented, Accepted, Draft, Rejected). Cite it before treating a CAP as protocol truth; a Draft describes an intention, not the network.

confidence.description: 0-1 trust signal: score, label (high/medium/low), relevance, freshness, authority, ageDays

docKind.description: Deterministic document class stamped at ingest: spec (canonical; old AND authoritative, e.g. SEPs/CAPs), guide (staleness-sensitive how-to), article, data. Null = not classified. Use it to weigh age: an old spec is still the truth, an old guide may not be.

docVersionStatus.description: SDK-version verdict for version-bearing content (e.g. a guide targeting wasm32-unknown-unknown is deprecated), from the same dated version table repo rows use. Null = the content names no version signal; not a claim it is current.

exactKeys.description: Present only when the query named an exact key (an audit finding id, a CVE or GHSA id, or a repo-qualified release tag): the named keys this row carries verbatim (a release tag by its release title). [] = this row carries none of them: for those keys it is a semantic neighbour, not the record. Absent = the query named no such key, or `fields` left it out.

observedAt.description: When ingest last crawled the page live

severity.description: Audit-source chunks only; section-inferred and CHUNK-level (labels the matched chunk's section, not the report or a finding), 'unknown' for most PDF-derived chunks

RetryableError.description: A failure the caller should retry: the read behind the answer failed (database, upstream, or this instance's rate window). Never a claim about the data; `advisory` says what the failure is NOT a claim about. Mirrors the Retry-After header in seconds.

advisory.description: What the failure is not a claim about, and what to do (retry after Retry-After, or where else to look).

hint.description: On a 429: the wait and the next step in words, the same number as retryAfterSeconds ('Wait 37 seconds, then resend the same request.'), for a consumer that keeps only error and hint.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Seconds to wait before resending; the same value as the Retry-After header. On a 429, the seconds until the rate window resets, or the language model's own wait (at most 3600, 60 when it sent no usable number); on a 503, 2 on database reads and 60 or 300 on the skills registry.

Rfp.description: An RFP row from /api/rfps. rowType discriminates real briefs from the synthetic live-round row; count/render briefs by filtering rowType === 'rfp'.

authorName.description: Sponsor/author of the brief; 'Stellar Community Fund' on synthetic rows.

category.description: Category slug: the ?category= filter vocabulary (an unrecognized filter value returns 400 with validCategories). 'scf' is carried by the synthetic live-round row.

id.description: Brief slug (also the stellarlight.xyz/ideas/{id} page). Synthetic rows use 'scf-round-{n}'.

publishedBrief.description: The brief SCF published for this idea on its RFP Track page: a commit-pinned copy of that page (the live page drops a quarter's briefs when the next arrive) and the day it was read. Absent: no published brief is linked, which is not a claim that SCF published none; always absent on synthetic scf-round rows.

functionalRequirements.description: The brief's functional requirements, restated short, in its order. Absent: not restated here; the brief at url has them, with its non-functional requirements, evaluation criteria and deliverables, which are not restated.

outOfScope.description: What the brief rules out of scope, restated short. Absent: not restated here.

title.description: The brief's title on the page.

quarter.description: Quarter slug (e.g. 'q1-2026'): the ?quarter= filter vocabulary. Synthetic rows carry the active quarter.

quarterLabel.description: Display label ('Q1 2026'); 'Live round' on synthetic rows.

rowType.description: 'rfp' = a curated sponsor brief. 'scf-round' = a SYNTHETIC row representing the live SCF round's open submission window (served as a row so row-reading agents don't miss the open round). Synthetic rows are NOT briefs: count/render briefs by filtering rowType === 'rfp'.

status.description: 'open' = the brief is still soliciting; not a claim that SCF submissions are open today (see meta.scfRound). 'closed' = a prior round, surfaced for context.

synthetic.description: True only on synthetic scf-round rows: mirror of rowType.

technicalRequirements.description: The idea's own summary of what to build, as stellarlight.xyz/ideas shows it: not the brief SCF published, and it can differ from it (some were written before the brief). The published brief is publishedBrief. Null when the idea carries none, and always null on synthetic scf-round rows.

url.description: Brief page (stellarlight.xyz/ideas/{id}); the SCF awards page on synthetic scf-round rows.

Skill.description: One installable Stellar AI skill/tool from /api/skills: SDF's skills.stellar.org set, curated entries, and approved community submissions mapped onto one unified shape. Optional fields are OMITTED when not applicable (absent = not applicable, never null and never false).

argumentHint.description: Registry entries only: argument hint (e.g. '[payment task]'). Absent elsewhere.

compatibility.description: Agent runtimes the skill is known to work in (e.g. 'Claude Code', 'Codex', 'Cursor').

docs.description: Docs URL. Absent on most rows.

featured.description: Editorially featured. Absent (not false) on most rows.

install.description: Primary install command, e.g. 'npx skills add https://github.com/stellar/stellar-dev-skill' for the SDF set (the registry's own command) or 'npx skills add <that repository>' for a community-built entry. Absent when the entry has no one-line install.

installAlt.description: Alternate install commands for other agent runtimes: an ARRAY of {label, command} entries (label = the runtime, e.g. 'Codex'). Absent when only the primary install applies.

rawUrl.description: Direct raw SKILL.md URL for entries listed on skills.stellar.org (SDF authored and community-built). Absent elsewhere.

registry.description: 'skills.stellar.org' when the entry is listed on SDF's registry (either section), including a curated entry the registry lists under another name. Absent for entries we curate or host that the registry does not list.

repository.description: Source repository URL. Absent when not published.

source.description: Who stands behind the entry. sdf = SDF authored (the registry's Included Stellar Skills section). community = community-built: listed on skills.stellar.org under its author's maintenance and not reviewed by SDF (registry present), or an approved submission to this directory (registry absent). stellarlight and lumenloop = curated by those teams; external = an SDK, CLI or tool we list.

tagline.description: One-line summary. Absent on some rows.

userInvocable.description: Registry entries only (SDF authored and community-built): whether the skill is user-invocable in skills.stellar.org's sense. Absent elsewhere.

SourcePointer.description: Where a fact lives in an allowlisted Stellar repo, never the content: fetch verificationUrl to read it. Names, a line and hashes only.

authorityRole.description: implementation = the repo's code (core, SDKs, host, RPC, quickstart, OpenZeppelin's contract library); tooling = stellar-cli; reference-docs = any Markdown file and the soroban-examples contracts. A role, not an endorsement.

blobSha.description: git blob id of the file at ref, the id GitHub serves for it: provenance, not security.

factors.description: Compact score parts: words matched of q, exact, prefix (an identifier held in the name), word, path, join (adjacent words of q matched as one name), ident (identifiers typed in q found whole, counted double), cmd (stellar-cli command words the file's module path matches), repo named, name (share of the name's own words q accounts for).

id.description: Short id within this response (s1, s2, ...), the same order as rank.

line.description: 1-based line the locator sits on at ref; null for a file pointer.

locator.description: The symbol name or heading text as written; null for a file pointer.

locatorKind.description: file = the whole file; symbol = a named definition (function, type, constant, CLI flag, config option or key, environment variable) or a Rust trait implementation, written impl Trait for Type; heading = a Markdown section.

matchReason.description: Which words of q matched and how, at most 100 characters.

rank.description: Position in the full ranking for this q (page 2 starts at 11). Array order is rank order.

ref.description: The 40-hex commit the pointer was read at. An unchanged file keeps its first ref: the same blob and lines hold at later commits up to the repo's indexed ref (meta.index).

score.description: 0 to 100 for this q and this pointer alone; compare within one response, not across queries.

verifiedAt.description: When the index build last confirmed this pointer's blob and line (its repo's builtAt); null only if that build time is unknown.

Stablecoin.description: One Stellar stablecoin from /api/stablecoins, measured every 6h from Horizon, Stellar Expert and live peg FX. marketCapUSD is the ONLY cross-row-comparable size metric; `supply` is raw units in the asset's own `peg`. null on any metric = not measured, never 'zero'. Identity is (code, issuer); two live assets can share a ticker (Circle's EURC and MyKobo's EURC are different assets), so never merge or match on `ticker` alone; join on `assetId` or `issuer`.

assetId.description: `CODE-<first 8 of issuer>`: the stable natural key, and the safe join key when a ticker is ambiguous.

assetType.description: Recorded only where the registry found the unit is not 1:1 with its peg; such rows are priced from their own market where it can be read (priceBasis). Yield Stablecoin = yield accrues to or is paid on the unit (Ondo's USDY); Treasury-Backed = a Treasury-backed bond (USDM1). Null = no qualifier recorded: the row was not classified, so null is unknown, NOT a verified plain peg and NOT 'not yield-bearing'. Filter with ?assetType=.

basis.description: How THIS row's numbers were obtained. live = measured this cycle. curated-static = hand-checked figures for an asset no public API reports reliably (an as-of estimate, NOT a live measurement; say so when citing). unmeasured = the fetch failed this cycle and the row is retained deliberately so its absence is never read as a delisting; its metrics are the last known values, dated by updatedAt.

company.description: The brand the asset is marketed under, as this registry curates it (Novatti Group for AUDD, Currency One for C1USD). A display name, NOT the legal issuer: for who issues the asset, read issuerOfRecord.

country.description: Home country code of the PEG currency (US for USD, EU for EUR), or Global, for flag display. It describes the peg, NOT the issuer's jurisdiction or place of incorporation.

issuer.description: Full mainnet issuer account (G…): the universal join key. With `ticker` this IS the asset's identity.

issuerDomain.description: The asset's web domain as this registry curates it (the logo is read from its stellar.toml). Not always the issuer account's on-chain home_domain; the issuer's own toml, the source of issuerOfRecord, is at issuerOfRecordSourceUrl.

issuerOfRecord.description: The legal issuer as the issuer publishes it: ORG_NAME in the stellar.toml at the issuer account's home_domain (from Horizon), counted only when that toml lists the account in ACCOUNTS or as a currency issuer, so both sides of the link agree (SEP-1). AUDD: AUDC PTY LTD. Set only when issuerOfRecordCheck is named; read by the 6-hourly writer, never at request time, and never derived from company. Cite it with issuerOfRecordAsOf.

issuerOfRecordAsOf.description: When the stored check was made. A failed read does not move it, so a date well before updatedAt means the latest runs could not reach the toml. Date issuerOfRecord by this, not by updatedAt. Null = never read.

issuerOfRecordCheck.description: What the stored check of that toml found. named = it lists the account and gives an ORG_NAME (issuerOfRecord). not-named = the read completed and named no issuer: the account sets no home_domain, or a stellar.toml was read there that does not list the account or gives no ORG_NAME (issuerOfRecordNote says which); a checked absence, dated by issuerOfRecordAsOf. null = never read. A read that could not be made changes nothing, so the stored check and its date stay as they were: a network failure or a body that fails mid-read, any HTTP error, a not found too (a lapsed or parked home_domain answers the same, so it does not prove the issuer stopped issuing), a redirect off the home_domain or to http, and a body over 100 KB or one that does not read as a stellar.toml (HTML, a Not Found text, a JSON error, an empty body). A toml read that cannot answer changes nothing either: an ORG_NAME in a form the parser cannot read, or an account the toml does not list where it holds a listing the parser cannot read (a currency linked to its own toml, a code it cannot read).

issuerOfRecordNote.description: On a named check: that toml's own desc for this currency, quoted, where it names an issuing party other than issuerOfRecord (MGUSD: 'issued by Bridge on behalf of MoneyGram'), else null. On a not-named check: why no issuer of record was named.

issuerOfRecordSourceUrl.description: The stellar.toml URL the stored check read, after same-host https redirects (https://<home_domain>/.well-known/stellar.toml unless the host moved it); re-verify there. Null when the account sets no home_domain or nothing was read yet.

logoSource.description: Provenance of logoUrl. toml = the issuer's own per-currency image. toml-org = the same toml's org-level mark, used when no per-currency image exists but the org one resolves. fallback = a hand-curated override. country-flag = the peg's flag IS the intended mark, not a stand-in. none = nothing resolved, logoUrl is null.

logoUrl.description: The issuer's own mark, when one resolves. Null means render your own fallback (e.g. a peg flag); absence is not itself an error.

marketCapUSD.description: Supply valued in USD (supply × priceUSD). THE comparable ranking metric (default sort). Null = unpriced. Read it with `priceBasis`: on an assumed-peg row this is supply at par, not a market valuation.

note.description: Plain-words reason a row is curated-static or unmeasured. Null for live rows.

paymentsCount24h.description: Count, not a dollar amount, of payment operations over the last 24 hours: Stellar Expert's lifetime payments counter diffed against our own reading of it from 20 to 28 hours earlier, the one nearest 24 hours (each row keeps two days of its six-hourly readings). Mint, redemption and peer-to-peer payments undifferentiated, not adjusted for exchange, DeFi or infrastructure activity. Null when no reading falls in that window, so also for about a day after the readings start; never a longer or shorter span, never 0 for no data.

peg.description: Fiat the asset tracks (USD, JPY, ARS, …). `supply` is in THIS unit, so raw supply is NOT comparable across rows with different pegs; use marketCapUSD.

priceBasis.description: How priceUSD was obtained. assumed-peg = the peg's live FX rate; the asset claims par and peg DEVIATION IS NOT MEASURED. measured-market = the unit's own market price, used where the unit is not 1:1 with its peg. Ondo's USDY accrues (it was $1.14 against a $1.00 peg on 2026-09-09) and USDM1 is a bond trading above par. Null exactly when priceUSD is null.

priceUSD.description: USD price of one unit. At the peg's live FX rate for a par-redeemable asset (≈1 for USD pegs); the token's own market price where the unit is NOT 1:1 with its peg. `priceBasis` says which; do not assume ≈1 on a USD row.

supply.description: Circulating supply in whole asset units of its own peg. NOT USD, NOT comparable across pegs. Null = not measured.

supplyChange7d.description: Percent change in supply vs our snapshot measured 6 to 8 days back, the one nearest 7 days (e.g. -5.8 means down 5.8%). Null when no snapshot falls in that window, never a longer span; never 0 for 'no data'.

ticker.description: Asset code (USDC, USDY, GYEN, …). NOT unique on its own: see assetId.

updatedAt.description: When these figures were measured (dated-metrics rule). Always cite it.

verified.description: True by construction: every issuer in the registry is hand-verified against the issuer's own domain. It does NOT discriminate between rows and is not a quality signal.

apiVersion.description: API contract (OpenAPI) version: equals /api/openapi.json info.version. Reason about the live contract from this rather than the service version.

populationId.description: Scope digest of what `count` counts: same format as meta.population.id on /api/analyze and /api/clusters. DB-backed sources here are `<collection>|status:all` (the FULL collection incl. Inactive), which is why projects.count is larger than analyze/clusters' active-only populations. Different ids = different populations: never merge or compare the numbers without labeling the scopes.

info.description:
Read-only public API powering Stellar Scout. Aggregators, autonomous agents, and AI tools can call these endpoints directly without auth.

All endpoints are edge-cached. The same data is available via the @stellar-light/scout-mcp Model Context Protocol server (for human-driven clients) and via the @stellar-light/api-client TypeScript SDK (for autonomous aggregators).

Data sources merged behind these endpoints: the Stellarlight directory of curated Stellar projects + an indexed-and-scored GitHub repo index, Stellar Passport builder profiles, Electric Capital developer activity, Soroban audit corpus, SDF skills.stellar.org skill catalog, lumenloop ecosystem data, and primary research (SEPs, papers, dev docs, SCF Handbook). Live collection sizes are in GET /api/status (sources[]); counts are intentionally not hardcoded here to avoid drift.

## Routing metadata (description vs x-routing)
Operation `description` fields are deliberately terse purpose statements: the operation's distinctive job plus its single sharpest disambiguation, nothing else. The machine-routing vocabulary that previously lived in description prose (category/product enumerations, synonym chains, example question phrasings) lives in each operation's `x-routing` extension: `{purpose, keywords[], useWhen[], notFor[], exampleQuestions[]}`. Lexical and embedding routers should score `x-routing` as separately-weighted fields rather than concatenating it into the description (broad prose descriptions were lexically capturing question families other operations answer); `notFor` entries name the operation to prefer, as '<question shape> -> <operationId>'.

## Versioning
Every response carries an `X-API-Version` header (currently `1`). The number bumps only on a breaking response-shape change; additive fields don't bump it. Pin to a version by asserting the header. Breaking changes are announced before they ship.

## Rate limits
Rate-limit counters are kept per serverless instance (every limited response carries X-RateLimit-Scope: instance), so X-RateLimit-Remaining and -Reset describe the instance that answered, not a global window. Per-IP, per-endpoint, per-minute floors on the cost-bearing routes (typically 60 requests a minute; `/api/research` 60 a minute), advertised on every response via `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and on a 429 via `Retry-After`. Cache where `Cache-Control` allows and prefer `offset` pagination over hammering. A platform whose users share one egress IP (an agent runtime, an MCP host) can ask support@stellarlight.xyz for a partner key: sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key`, it is metered per key instead of per IP, at 1,200 requests a minute and 200,000 a day. A 503 (store or index unavailable) carries `Retry-After` in seconds. `/api/research` also answers `X-Scout-Match-Mode` (`vector` or `keyword`, the same value as `meta.matchMode`) and `Server-Timing` (our wall time in ms), and when it falls back to keyword its `meta.warnings` says why.

## Pagination
List endpoints (`/api/projects/search`, `/api/builders`, `/api/rfps`) accept `limit` + `offset`. EVERY list response carries `meta.counts` with `returned` (this page) and `total`/`matched` (all rows matching the filter, pre-slice); compare the two to tell a complete read from a truncated one, and page until `offset + returned >= total`. Two documented exceptions, both explicit rather than silent: `searchResearch` serves `total: null` with a `totalBasis` because similarity ranking has no crisp matching set, and `/api/changelog` additionally serves `returned`/`total` flat on `meta` for backward compatibility; those flat fields are DEPRECATED, read `meta.counts`. `searchRepos` ranks a capped candidate window (the top 200 rows by repoScore for a browse with no q, the top 600 for a search): when `meta.counts.truncated` is true, `total` counts that window and paging ends there, and `meta.counts.eligible` gives the number of rows the filters admit (null where only ranking every row could count them).

## Ordering & relevance
`/api/projects/search` sorts by descending keyword `score` (token-overlap count) and exposes `meta.matchMode` (`strict` → `loose-1` → `majority` → `semantic`) so you know how much the query was relaxed. `semantic` means no keyword tier matched at all; the rows are vector-similarity guesses (`via: "semantic"`, confidence capped at medium), not keyword-confirmed answers. When `?type=` is present, TYPE DEFINES MEMBERSHIP (the full typed set, limit-independent) and q only ranks within it; matchMode reports `all` with an explicit label, because a tier would falsely claim q gated the set (sls-033). `corrected` means the rows matched ONLY through a known spelling correction (e.g. strupey → stroopy): the query token does not occur in the rows, so verify the identity before treating them as evidence about the queried name. `/api/research` sorts by descending vector-similarity `score` (0-1 cosine). Use these for cross-source ranking when merging with other aggregators.
info.summary: Agent-native data layer for the Stellar ecosystem: projects, builders, hackathons, SCF, audits, research.
info.title: Stellar Scout API

get.description: The cross-ecosystem macro rollup: totals no single-event tool answers. Slice via `dimension=hackathons|categories|funding|tvl|gaps|developers|toolchain`: hackathon + SCF-funding totals, category distribution, DeFi TVL (dated), `gaps` (per-vertical whitespace: what should I build), `developers` (Electric Capital monthly-active devs + trend), and `toolchain` (Soroban-SDK version-status distribution + deprecated-toolchain roster + CI/test presence). gaps/developers/toolchain are SUPPLY/commit-side and as-of dated; never demand or a headcount.

parameters.description: Which slice to return
parameters.name: dimension

categories.description: Present for dimension=all|categories: project counts by category over the active population (see meta.population).

developers.description: Present for dimension=all|developers: Electric Capital ecosystem developer counts with their snapshot date; cite the snapshot date, not generatedAt.

asOf.description: Electric Capital snapshot date: cite THIS, not generatedAt.

exclusive.description: Devs building ONLY on Stellar: the truer measure of committed builders.

peerChains.description: Peer-chain MAD for scale context, not a quality ranking.

funding.description: Present for dimension=all|funding. Carries computedAt, methodologyVersion, countBasis, byRound, and projectSetHash: a stable sha256-prefix digest of the sorted awarded-project slug set. Same hash across your snapshots ⇒ same project SET (only amounts/labels can differ); different hash ⇒ membership changed (adds/removals/reclassifications): the honest explanation for a moving cumulative total under an unchanged methodology. #520 delta provenance: snapshotAsOf / previousSnapshot / snapshotDelta make the set change ANSWER-VISIBLE: which slugs were added/removed vs the preceding persisted snapshot and mechanical reason codes for removals; deltaBasis documents the semantics and deltaUnavailable states explicitly when the comparison cannot be served (no differing prior snapshot yet, or store unavailable).

byRound.description: Per-round totals (round number, projects, USD): the breakdown scfCountBasis points at.

count.description: Per-round MEMBERSHIP: a project counts in each round it won, so summing counts exceeds scfAwardedProjects.

computedAt.description: When THIS response's funding rollup was computed.

countBasis.description: Plain-language statement of what the funding numbers count (in-house rollup basis vs SDF's own counters).

deltaUnavailable.description: Non-null when snapshotDelta cannot be served, stating WHY: no valid differing prior snapshot is stored (empty or incomplete ones are skipped), the most recent stored snapshots read hold no other set, this read found no awarded project or was truncated (it is then neither stored nor compared), or the snapshot store is unavailable; an explicit reason, never a silent omission.

postHackathonStatusFunnel.description: Outcome funnel for hackathon-linked active projects. Besides `scope`, keys are post-hackathon status names (Built / In Progress / Abandoned / Unknown, plus any other recorded status) mapping to project counts.

scope.description: Which projects the funnel tallies (hackathon-linked only, with the population size).

previousSnapshot.description: The most recent persisted snapshot with a DIFFERENT project set whose stored slug list is non-empty and reproduces its projectSetHash: an empty or incomplete stored snapshot is never a baseline. Null when none is found (see deltaUnavailable).

scfAwardedProjects.description: Projects in the awarded set this rollup sums over.

scfTotalDistributedUSD.description: Sum of scfTotalAwardedUSD over the awarded set; an in-house rollup; reconcile per-project via scfRoundAwards.

snapshotAsOf.description: When the CURRENT projectSetHash was first observed (persisted snapshot time). computedAt is when THIS response was computed; snapshotAsOf dates the set state. Null when this read is neither stored nor compared (deltaUnavailable says why).

snapshotDelta.description: Membership diff: this response's awarded set vs previousSnapshot's. Null when previousSnapshot is null (deltaUnavailable says why).

addedProjects.description: Slugs in the current set but not the previous snapshot.

removedReasons.description: Per removed slug, a MECHANICAL reason from the record's current state; never a guess.

reason.description: 'dedupe' = record now points at a canonical slug (duplicate merged); 'eligibility-reclassification' = record left the active status pool; 'source-correction' = scf.awarded corrected to false; 'unknown' = record missing or no mechanical signal.

totalUSDDelta.description: This response's scfTotalDistributedUSD minus the previous snapshot's.

gaps.description: Present for dimension=gaps: whitespace analysis; product types unproven/underbuilt/absent in the active population. SUPPLY-side evidence only, never demand proof.

byType.description: Every vertical (incl. absent ones) with its coverage, thinnest first.

hackathons.description: Present for dimension=all|hackathons: cross-event rollup from the live DoraHacks feed. null (dimension=all only) = the DoraHacks read failed this request: unknown, never zero; meta.warnings says so and the response is not cached. dimension=hackathons answers 503 instead.

dimension.description: The dimension this response was computed for.

validDimensions.description: Every value the dimension param accepts (unknown values 400 with this list).

warnings.description: Present only when a block of a dimension=all response is null because its read failed this request (today: hackathons): what is missing, and that it is unknown, not zero.

toolchain.description: Soroban SDK toolchain health across scanned repos: how many run supported / current / deprecated SDK versions, with the deprecated rows named. Present for dimension=all|toolchain.

deprecatedListTruncated.description: true = deprecatedRepos is a capped sample (50) and shorter than deprecatedTotal; never read its length as the count.

engineeringPractice.description: Repos whose latest scan recorded tree-level CI and test presence: presence facts only, not CI results.

measuredRepos.description: How many repos byVersionStatus was actually computed over. Equal to scannedRepos when measurementComplete is true; smaller when the scan hit its cap. THIS is the denominator for any rate.

measurementComplete.description: false = the buckets describe only part of the population; a rate taken against scannedRepos would understate every status.

vertical.description: Detected buildable vertical (closed set from the gaps axis); null = unmapped, not marketless.

vet.description: Same computation as /api/vet-idea: competitors, maturity, judged prior art, and the supply-side gap row.

matchMode.description: How relevance was established for the served projects: vertical = typed membership; vertical+scored = typed members plus rows that scored on the idea's own terms; scored = an anchor token matched; weak = generic words only (rows are neighbours, not evidence a competitor exists) or no project matched enough of the idea (projects is empty, which is not evidence that none exists). When the idea uses two or more words the directory knows, every served project matches a minimum share of their weight (rarer words weigh more), so fewer than 8 can be served.

status.description: The project's directory status, read live with this response; not dated per row.

via.description: How the row qualified: vertical = a typed member of the idea's vertical; scored = it matched the idea's own words. Absent when the idea maps to no vertical.

tier.description: The repo's grade tier, read live from the index with this response; not dated per row.

gap.description: SUPPLY-side coverage of the idea's vertical: a gap is not demand. Null when no vertical mapped.

builds.description: null = the submissions index could not be read (not checked; the note says so), [] = checked, none listed (read it with buildsBelowEvidenceRule). Stored hackathon submissions matching the idea, best first: searchHackathonBuilds in hybrid mode (words plus meaning), across events on DoraHacks and off it. When buildsReranked is true, the first 50 of that ranking are reordered by a reranker that reads the idea with each build's name and summary, and of its top five the builds it scores at least 0.45 are listed. When it is false, of the hybrid top five only builds with a score of at least 0.7, two matched words, or every word of the idea the search reads used in the build's own name or description (a synonym, track or award text does not count; the search skips generic words such as app, so a one-word idea's builds need only mention that word) are listed. `matchedTerms` shows which words matched; `similarity` is the meaning score; a build with similarity and no matchedTerms was found by meaning alone, and a reranked build with neither by the reranker alone, so check it.

similarity.description: Meaning similarity to the idea, 0 to 1; absent when search by meaning did not run.

buildsBelowEvidenceRule.description: How many of the five nearest submissions are not in builds because they fell short of the evidence rule (the reranker's 0.45 when buildsReranked is true). builds [] with a count above 0 means submissions came close but none met the rule (the note says so; searchHackathonBuilds with the same q lists them), not that nobody built this; builds [] with 0 means nothing came close. null with builds when the index could not be read.

buildsMode.description: The search that served builds: hybrid normally, keyword when search by meaning could not run (the note then says so); null with builds when the index could not be read.

buildsReranked.description: true = the hybrid ranking's first 50 were reordered by a reranker (a cross-encoder model) that reads the idea with each build's name and summary, and builds holds the builds of its top five it scored at least 0.45. false = the reranker did not run: buildsMode is keyword, no submission matched, or it failed, took longer than 2 s, or was skipped because search by meaning had already taken longer than 3 s (the note then says which), so builds is the hybrid top five under the word and meaning rule. null with builds when the index could not be read.

whatNotToClaim.description: Deterministic cautions derived from THIS brief's own facts; each names the fact it stands on. Empty when the brief gives no reason for one.

400.description: Bad or unknown query param.

429.description: This endpoint's rate window is spent. hint states the wait in seconds and the next step; retryAfterSeconds and Retry-After carry the same number. Counters are per serverless instance (X-RateLimit-Scope: instance), so a host-wide window read from the headers is approximate. It says nothing about the data: wait, then resend the same request.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; the same number as retryAfterSeconds.

Server-Timing.description: Our own wall time, as on a 200.

X-RateLimit-Scope.description: Always `instance`: the counter is per serverless instance, not global.

Shares are over known values. Unit: event entries (a submission in two events counts twice). Same filters as searchHackathonBuilds; for the builds themselves → use searchHackathonBuilds.

parameters.description: What to count (default category). category: directory project types. library: the Stellar libraries a repo builds on (renamed and sibling packages folded together). package: the exact packages a repo declares. activity: commits on the submitted repo 90+ days after the event, archived, or repo not found. project: became a directory project (a floor). projectStatus: that project's directory status today. scf: whether SCF funded it. placement: winner or not. track, event, year.

parameters.description: Report only this value (Payments, soroban-sdk), as a row even at zero. With by=event: the trend of one value. With facet=library a package name counts as the library it belongs to (soroban-sdk = Soroban Rust SDK). A value no stored submission carries adds a meta.warnings line naming the values seen: its 0 is a miss, not a measured count.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: Most values to report per set (default 10, or 5 with by; max 30).
parameters.name: top

parameters.description: Topic: count only the submissions that match it, the way searchHackathonBuilds matches, except that a declared package does not match here. A word only a declared package uses still counts as used when deciding whether most of q's words occur in no submission, which holds back builds matched by name alone. Empty = every submission.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: How q matches (default: keyword). keyword: the query's words, stems and synonyms. meaning: vector similarity over each submission's name, summary and write-up, for ideas phrased differently from how teams described them. hybrid: both, blended. If search by meaning cannot run, keyword results are served and meta.warnings says so (meta.mode.served).
parameters.name: mode

parameters.description: Set to 1 for prize winners only: the winners DoraHacks assigned and those a page off DoraHacks names (getHackathon shows these with winnerSource), by words and by meaning alike. Accepts 1/true/yes/on (and 0/false/no/off for explicit off); any other value returns 400 with the accepted forms, never silently ignored.
parameters.name: winnersOnly

parameters.description: Only these events: up to 10, comma-separated, each an event's slug or its exact title, any case. An event getHackathons lists whose submissions are not stored matches nothing, and meta.warnings says so; a value that names no event getHackathons lists answers 400 with validHackathons, the slugs of every event with stored submissions. A submission can enter several events; under this filter each row is that event's own entry, with its own placement.
parameters.name: hackathon

parameters.description: Filter by hackathon track (substring match).
parameters.name: track

parameters.description: Only submissions sorted into this directory project type. Submissions not categorized yet are left out, so the set is a floor.
parameters.name: category

parameters.description: Only builds whose repo declares this Stellar package, exact name (passkey-kit, soroban-sdk, @x402/stellar). Builds whose repo was not read are left out, so the set is a floor, not everyone who used it.
parameters.name: package

groups.description: Present with `by`: the facet within each group. Events and years run oldest first; a group where nothing matched reports zero.

coverage.description: by=event only, present only when the event's stored rows are its winners alone (winners-only), which happens only when such rows are all the set holds: its counts describe its winners, the size and mix of its field are unknown, and every share in the group is null.

field.description: Builds in this group before q: the group's whole field. On a group with coverage winners-only, the event's winners on record, not its field, and every share in the group is null.

known.description: Builds whose value is known: every share's denominator.

unknown.description: Builds whose value is unknown (meta.facet.unknownMeans): never counted as none.

share.description: builds / known (0 to 1); null when no build's value is known, or when the counted rows are incomplete (only a winners-only event's winners): no share is computed over them.

indexedBuilds.description: Event entries in the index. A submission entered in several events counts once per event.

measured.description: facet=category only: each reported type's precision and recall, measured leave-one-out on the hand-typed directory at its cut. A type with low recall undercounts; balanced precision and recall track its true share.

unknownMeans.description: Why a build's value can be unknown; null when it never is.

filters.description: The filters as applied: an echo, so a caller can see what was honoured.

hackathon.description: The slugs the hackathon values resolved to; a value that could not be checked against the event listing (meta.warnings names it) is echoed as sent, lowercased. null = no hackathon filter.

matchMode.description: How submissions matched q: filtered = the query's words (with stems and synonyms); vector = similarity in meaning; hybrid = both; all = no q.

warnings.description: Present only when something limited this answer, e.g. counting by meaning, or a hackathon value that names an event whose submissions are not stored ('no submissions are stored for <slug>') or could not be checked ('could not check hackathon ...'). Either hackathon line means 0 counted from that event is not evidence that nothing was built. No rate is computed over incomplete rows (an event whose stored rows are its winners only). When the set also holds full listings, those rows are left out of every count and share, and one line names the events and the rows left out ('left out of every count and share: 12 rows of <slug> (6), ...'), so facet=event and by=event do not list those events. A value only left-out rows carry serves its 0 with every share null (in total, in a group holding those rows and in winnersVsOthers), and a line names it (value '<v>': only rows left out above carry it ...). When they are all the set holds (a hackathon value naming only such events, or filters that leave only them), their counts stay, every share is null, and a line names them ('only the winners of <slug> are stored ...').

total.description: The facet over every matched submission, less the incomplete rows meta.warnings says were left out.

field.description: Builds passing every filter except q, less incomplete rows left out (meta.warnings); builds / field is the share that matched q. When only a winners-only event's rows are counted, they are its winners, not its field.

known.description: Builds whose value is known: every share's denominator.

unknown.description: Builds whose value is unknown (meta.facet.unknownMeans): never counted as none.

share.description: builds / known (0 to 1); null when no build's value is known, or when the counted rows are incomplete (only a winners-only event's winners): no share is computed over them.

winnersVsOthers.description: Winners against everyone else in the matched set, value by value, most common among winners first. Absent when the set has no winners or no others, or facet=placement, or when the set is only a winners-only event's rows. Incomplete rows left out of the set (meta.warnings) are not among the winners.

lift.description: winnersShare / othersShare: above 1 = more common among winners. null when either share is unknown or zero. Small counts are noise.

200.description: The facet counted over the filtered submissions.

error.description: What was wrong, naming the value.

supportedParams.description: Every parameter the operation reads; sent with an unknown parameter.

validHackathons.description: The slug of every event with stored submissions, alphabetical (the order means nothing); sent when a hackathon value names no event getHackathons lists. Pass one of these, or the event's exact title. getHackathons lists every event; one whose submissions are not stored is accepted and matches nothing, with a meta.warnings line.

validValues.description: The values the named parameter accepts.

400.description: A parameter or value the operation cannot honour; fix the call, do not retry it as is. The body names it and lists what would work: supportedParams for an unknown parameter, validValues for a value outside an enumerated parameter's set, validHackathons for a hackathon value that names no event getHackathons lists.

503.description: The index could not be built; retry after Retry-After.

get.description: Topic search across every stored Stellar hackathon submission ('buidl') on DoraHacks: the PROTOTYPE layer of prior art. Answers 'has anyone built X at a hackathon?' with each build's event, placement, repo/demo links, `project` (the directory project listing its exact repo) and `stack`. meta.stack counts the Stellar SDKs the matched repos declare: winnersOnly=1 = which SDKs winners use. Winners first among equals; in hybrid mode a reranker orders the top 50. Unit: submissions (counts.entries = event entries). Absence is a whitespace signal, not proof. For SHIPPED products → use searchProjects.

parameters.description: Topic to search build names, descriptions and the packages their repos declare (prior-art lookup). A build is listed when it covers half of q's words, or when its name holds one of them unless most of q's words occur as a whole word in no submission (text or declared packages). A word of four letters or more also matches inside a longer word. In a question (q ends with ? or opens with which, who, whom, whose, what, where, when, why, how, has, have, had, did, does, do, is, are, was, were, can, could, will, would or should, followed by a space), the question marks and the words that ask about an outcome or the past rather than a topic (won, win, wins, winner, winners, winning, prize, prizes, award, awards, awarded, placed, hackathon, hackathons, built, builds, past, ever, previous, previously, anyone, someone, already, before) are not searched, unless they are all q holds. When any of q's words occurs as a whole word in no submission, meta.warnings names those words and says what the listed builds are, and says when a build whose name matched was held back (meta.counts.withheldByName). With no hackathon parameter, an event named in full in q (its title, in any case, accents and punctuation aside, or its slug, hyphens included, in any case) becomes the hackathon filter and leaves q (meta.inferredFilter). The rest of q is searched inside that event; a rest made only of words the search skips (stopwords and generic words such as app, token, crypto, money, stellar, github) and words that ask for the event's entries (winners, builds, projects, places, awards, rankings) lists the event as the filter alone does. When the rest matches none of the event's rows and none of them holds a description, meta.warnings says so. A name start several events share infers nothing; meta.warnings names those events. Any hackathon parameter turns this off: send hackathon= with no value to search the words as text in every event.

parameters.description: Skip this many matched builds (default 0). To read every match, page with limit and offset until offset + meta.counts.returned reaches meta.counts.matched; pages share one ranking.
parameters.name: offset

afterEvent.description: What the submitted repo did after the event, in analyzeHackathonSubmissions' activity vocabulary: a commit 90 or more days after the event ended, none by then, archived, or the repo not found. Absent = unknown: the repo's activity was not read, the event has no usable end date (missing or unreadable), or it ended under 90 days ago with no commit past that mark. It describes the submitted repo, not the project: work can move to another repo and a live product can sit still in code, so read `project.status` before calling a build dead.

award.description: This build's own award as DoraHacks published it: one award per winner ('1st Place - $5,000'), or one prize several winners each won. null = not a winner, no award named, or an award that names a category (`awardCategory`); what this build won is then `placement` and `prizeUsd`.

awardCategory.description: The award this build placed in, when its title names a category or pool, never this build's prize: its event's winners of other placements share it, or the title states more than this build's placement. All five Real-World ZK winners share '$10,000 XLM Prize' while placing 1st ($5,000) to 5th ($750). null = no other placement of this event is served under the award and its title states no more than this build's placement, so the award, if any, reads as the build's own.

categories.description: Directory project types this build was sorted into, best first. Present only when categorized; scores and method are on getHackathonSubmission.

hackathonSlug.description: The event's slug, the one getHackathons lists and getHackathon opens.

id.description: Opens the full submission in getHackathonSubmission.

isWinner.description: Placed in the event; absence of a win is not a quality judgement.

lastCommitAt.description: The submitted repo's last commit on its default branch when it was last read; null = read, no commit date. Absent = the repo's activity was not read (a repo not found has none to read).

matchedTerms.description: Which query terms this build matched: the evidence behind its inclusion. A term matches in the name, summary, track, award or award category, or a package in `stack`, except the Stellar JS SDK, Soroban Rust SDK, Freighter API, Stellar Wallets Kit and x402 packages, which more than a tenth of read repos declare. A package says what a build was made with, not what it does, so only this operation matches packages: prior art in vetIdea and hackathonBrief, and analyzeHackathonSubmissions' q, read the text alone.

placement.description: This build's own placement inside its award category ('1st Place', '3rd Place') as DoraHacks published it; null = placed without a rank or not a winner.

prizeUsd.description: What this build itself won in USD, parsed from its own placement string; null = not stated there, never 0. An `award` of its own can name the amount ('1st Place - $5,000'); an `awardCategory` names a category or pool, never this build's amount.

project.description: The directory project this build became, or null when none is found. Linked when a project lists the build's exact GitHub repo; when none does, when the build's demo site is a project's own website; and when neither, when the build's repo sits under the project's GitHub owner and the build carries the project's name (`basis` says which). The two repo rules also read the repo GitHub now redirects githubUrl to, when the team renamed or transferred it. A winner none of those link can still link when its name is the name of exactly one project and a page says so too: the project's SCF page links this build's DoraHacks page, or the build's DoraHacks page lists the project's website or X account. A shared GitHub owner alone, a name alone, or a shared platform never counts. Absent = not checked (served from a live DoraHacks read), which is not the same as null.

basis.description: repo: the project lists this exact repo. website: the demo site is the project's website. owner-and-name: the repo sits under the project's GitHub owner and the build's name is the project's name, or starts with it. moved-repo: the repo was renamed or transferred (githubUrl redirects on GitHub), and the project lists the repo it moved to. moved-owner-and-name: owner-and-name, read on the repo it moved to. A repo GitHub could not find is never taken as moved. The last two link winners only, when the build's name (a trailing 'Stellar' aside) is the name or an alias of exactly one project: scf-page-and-name: the project's SCF page (scfSourceUrl on searchProjects) links this build's DoraHacks page. submission-links-and-name: this build's DoraHacks page lists the project's website or X account. Absent on links stored before the basis was recorded (all by repo).

factsReadAt.description: When status and scfAwarded were read from the directory (with the submissions index, at most an hour before this response). Absent with them.

scfAwarded.description: Whether SCF funded the project. Absent when it could not be read (unknown).

status.description: The project's directory status today. Absent when it could not be read (unknown).

security.description: Present only when this build's repo is held for malware (the repo's own hold is getRepoTrust `security`): the build is still served, but its GitHub link and repo name are withheld (null) and `note` says what not to do, in Scout's words. Absent means no hold on record, which is not a claim that the repo is safe.

similarity.description: Vector similarity to the query (0 to 1), present when mode was meaning or hybrid and the build cleared the floor. A row with similarity and no matchedTerms was found by meaning alone: verify it.

stack.description: Stellar packages this build's repo declares in its package.json and Cargo.toml files (soroban-sdk, @stellar/stellar-sdk, ...). Present only when the repo was read: absent = unknown (no repo link, not public, or not read yet); [] = declares none.

counts.description: returned vs total: how much the filters narrowed.

entries.description: Event entries that match: a submission entered in several events counts once per event. analyzeHackathonSubmissions counts this unit, so for the same filters and mode its total.builds equals this, not matched, with two exceptions that count here and not in analyze: a declared package q matched, and a winners-only event's rows analyze leaves out beside full listings (its meta.warnings names them).

indexedBuilds.description: Submissions in the index. A submission entered in several events counts once.

matched.description: Unique submissions that match: the rows this search pages through.

withheldByName.description: Builds whose name matched q but that are not listed, because most of the words searched in q occur as a whole word in no submission; meta.warnings names the words they matched. Not counted in matched or entries. 0 = none held back; always 0 in meaning mode, which never lists a build by its name.

filters.description: The filters as applied: an echo, so a caller can see what was honoured.

hackathon.description: The slugs the hackathon values resolved to; a value that could not be checked against the event listing (meta.warnings names it) is echoed as sent, lowercased. null = no hackathon filter.

inferredFilter.description: Present only when q named one event in full (its title, or its slug with its hyphens, in any case) and no hackathon parameter was sent: that event was applied as the hackathon filter (meta.filters.hackathon) and its name removed from q (meta.filters.q holds the rest, null when nothing was left to search). Absent = nothing was inferred. To search the words as text in every event instead, send hackathon= with no value.

hackathon.description: The slug of the event q named.

matched.description: The words of q read as its name, as sent.

matchMode.description: How rows matched q: filtered = the query's words (with stems and synonyms); vector = similarity in meaning; hybrid = both blended; all = no text query (structured filters only).

mode.description: The search mode asked for and the one that served. They differ only when search by meaning could not run.

reranked.description: Present only with q when hybrid served and a build matched. true = the first 50 of the hybrid ranking (word coverage blended with meaning, winners first among near equals) were reordered by a reranker, a cross-encoder that reads q with each build's name and summary together; it does not read placement, so a winner keeps no edge there except on a tie, and rows past 50 keep the hybrid order. false = the reranker failed, took longer than 2 s, or was skipped because search by meaning had already taken longer than 3 s, so every row is in hybrid order (meta.warnings says which). Absent = not attempted: no q, keyword or meaning mode, no matched build, or no reranker configured. Each page is ranked by its own request: when paging, read this flag on every page, since a page served after a failure is in hybrid order and its rows can repeat or skip rows of a reranked page.

stack.description: Which Stellar packages the matched builds' repos declare, over every matched build (not just this page). winnersOnly=1 with no q = what winners build on; add q for a topic.

buildsRead.description: Matched builds whose repo was read; packages are counted over these.

upstream.description: Where the raw builds came from (DoraHacks).

warnings.description: Present only when something limited this answer: search by meaning could not run, the reranker could not run or was skipped ('the reranker could not run this request ...' or 'the reranker was skipped because search by meaning took longer than 3 s ...'; rows are then in hybrid order), a hackathon value names an event whose submissions are not stored ('no submissions are stored for <slug>'), the event listing could not be read to check a hackathon value ('could not check hackathon ...'), or a word searched in q occurs as a whole word in no submission ('<n> of the <m> words searched in q (<words>) occur as a whole word in no submission in the index ...'; when every word does, 'the word searched in q ...' or 'none of the <m> words searched in q ...'). Either hackathon line means 0 matched from that event is not evidence that nothing was built. A hackathon value naming an event whose stored rows are its winners only adds 'only the winners of <slug> are stored ...': its rows are its winners, not its field. The q line says what the rows are: a build listed by its words (matchedTerms) matches only q's other words, or holds the named words only inside longer words when every word is absent; a build with similarity is close to q as a whole, not to the named words. It names related forms some submission does use ('a related form is used: cash for cashing'). When builds whose name matched q were held back because most of q's words occur in no submission, it says so ('1 build matched by name for donations is not listed, because most of the words searched in q occur in no submission'; a word found only inside a longer word of a name is named as 'inside a longer word for llama'); counts.withheldByName counts them. When nothing is listed it adds 'no build is listed; if one of them is misspelled, correct it', and names a used word ('remittance is a used word one edit from remitance') only when the word has five or more letters and no related form, and the used word is one edit away (a letter added, dropped or changed, or two adjacent letters swapped), starts with the same letter, is not a prefix of the word nor the word of it, and is the only such word or is used at least five times as often as any other. An event named in q adds one line, first: 'q holds the event name ...' when it became the filter (meta.inferredFilter), with the opt-out; 'q holds '<words>', the start of the names of <n> events (<slugs>) ...' or 'q names <n> events (<slugs>) ...' when nothing was inferred and q was searched as text; 'q names the event ... which hackathon= does not select ...' when an explicit hackathon filter won. When the rest of q matched none of an inferred event's stored submissions, none of them holds a description and no other filter (track, package, category, winnersOnly) narrowed the search, a line says so ('<rest>' matched no stored submission of <slug>: its <n> stored submissions hold no description to search; hackathon=<slug> alone lists them): that 0 says the rows hold nothing to search, not that nothing of the kind was built.

scfAwarded.description: Whether SCF funded the project. Absent when it could not be read (unknown).

status.description: The project's directory status today. Absent when it could not be read (unknown).

repo.description: owner/name from the GitHub link; null for an account or org link, or when the repo is held (see `security`).
