get.description: Feedback on one Stellar hackathon submission from its GitHub repo or DoraHacks link, no sign-in: its stored facts (Stellar packages, category, repo activity after the event, the directory project it became with status and SCF funding), checks that each state a fact (ok null = could not be checked), the submissions closest in meaning, and the SCF pitch view (live round, funded peers, competitors, prior art). hackathon=<slug> adds its judging criteria with the repo's evidence, read live, even for a repo not stored. Evidence, not a verdict. For an idea with no link → use vetIdea or scfPitch.

parameters.description: The submission's GitHub repo (owner/name or its URL) or its DoraHacks link or id. A repo submitted more than once resolves to its placed entry, then the newest. With hackathon, a GitHub repo with no stored submission is read live instead of answering 404.
parameters.name: link

parameters.description: An event whose judging criteria Scout holds as data. Adds review.judging: each of the event's criteria, in its record's words, with the evidence a judge would find in the repo, or checkable false with the reason (decks, videos, submission answers and intake goals are not read). The repo is read live from GitHub at its default branch's newest commit: read-only, inside 4 seconds, cached 5 minutes per repo, at most 20 such requests a minute per IP address (a partner key has its own tier), and never past a repo that is not public. One caller may spend at most a quarter of a server's hourly live-read budget; past it, its reads answer could-not-check. Any other value answers 400 with validHackathons.
parameters.name: hackathon

categoryContext.description: How crowded the submission's top category is across every stored submission of events whose full listing is stored: a winners-only event's winners are left out, so no share mixes them in. null when it has no confident category or is not categorized yet; categoryNote says which.

outOf.description: The share's denominator: the stored submissions in this scope (events whose full listing is stored) that have a category read, a confident type or none.

uncategorized.description: The stored submissions in this scope not categorized yet, outside outOf.

categoryNote.description: Why categoryContext is null: the submission has no confident category (uncertain, not missing), or it is not categorized yet. null when categoryContext is served.

checks.description: Mechanical checks over the submission's own facts, each a finding with its evidence. Not dated per item: the submission's own read dates (stackReadAt, activityCheckedAt, writeUpReadAt, project.factsReadAt) date them.

ok.description: true = in place; false = missing or a warning sign; null = could not be checked, never a no.

eventCategories.description: The submission's category within each event it entered, counted by analyzeHackathonSubmissions' category facet over that event's stored submissions: one entry per event, served even when the submission has no confident category of its own (thisCategory null). categories are the event's five largest, most submissions first. An event whose stored rows are its winners only, or whose winners are published in part, keeps its counts with every share null and submissions, categorized and uncategorized null, and note says why.

share.description: submissions / categorized; null over incomplete rows.

categorized.description: Of those, the ones with a category read (a confident type or none): every share's denominator.

note.description: Present only when the event's rows are incomplete: why its size and shares are not served.

submissions.description: The event's stored submissions; null when its rows are incomplete (note).

thisCategory.description: This submission's top category in the event; null when it has no confident category (categoryNote says why).

uncategorized.description: Of those, the ones not categorized yet.

judging.description: Present only with hackathon: each of the event's judging criteria by category, in its record's words (getHackathon serves the sentence as rules.judgingCriteria), with the evidence a judge would find in the repo, or checkable false with the reason, and the organizer's weighted rubric (rubric) when it publishes one. Evidence, not a verdict: no score, no pass or fail; the rubric's weights are the organizer's, never a score of this repo. Categories and criteria keep the sentence's order; the order is not a rank.

category.description: A category the event judges entries in (getHackathon tracks with kind category).

checkable.description: false: judged from what Scout does not read (pitch deck, demo video, submission answers, goals set at pre-event intake); reason says which, and evidence is null.

criterion.description: In the judging sentence's own words.

evidence.description: The facts that bear on the criterion; null when not checkable. One fact can serve several criteria and repeats in each.

count.description: The total behind values (test files following a convention, a floor of the repo's tests; CI files; releases; commits on the default branch; contract ids; Stellar packages; contract crates). null when not counted, and whenever the part read was partial (a manifest unread, the tree listing or the README cut short, a git submodule the tree read does not open), since a count over part of the repo is not its total; the finding then says what was not read. The test-file count is a floor either way, so it stays over a partial tree and the finding says at least.

finding.description: One sentence: the fact, what was read, and what was not.

id.description: stellarPackages: Stellar packages its manifests declare (Scout's list). contractCrates: Cargo.toml crates building a deployable Soroban contract. contractIds: contract ids the README names, not checked on chain. testFiles: files that follow a test-naming convention (the finding lists the conventions; a test named otherwise is not counted). ciConfig: CI config files. releases: GitHub releases. website: the repo's website field, whatever it points at, not opened and not called a demo. demoLinks: README links Scout reads as labelled a demo or live app (by its label words; a link labelled otherwise is not listed, a link whose words say docs is not a demo, and links inside HTML comments are not read), not opened. lastCommit: commits on the default branch and the last one's date. scfRound: the live SCF round state from communityfund.stellar.org, the source scfPitch reads.

state.description: found: read and present. not-found: read and absent, only within what the finding says was read. could-not-check: not read (GitHub did not answer, the budget was spent, a file was cut short, or a link could not be judged); never a no. Not dated here: every item rests on the one live read, dated by review.repo.readAt at the commit in review.repo.commit.

values.description: The cited values as written (package names, crate directories, contract ids, file paths, the latest release tag, URLs, the last commit's ISO date, open SCF rounds); a sample when count is larger. [] with not-found; null with could-not-check.

reason.description: Why it cannot be checked from the repo; null when checkable.

rubric.description: Curated events only: the weighted rubric the organizer publishes, each criterion with its weight in percent in the page's order (not a rank), each scored scoreMin to scoreMax, with the page and day it was checked. Absent: no weighted rubric is on record for this event, which is not a claim that the organizer published none.

byCategory.description: Present only on a slot scored under a different name in each category: one entry per category the event judges in (getHackathon tracks with kind category), with the criterion's name there and what it scores. Absent: the criterion is the same in every category.

scores.description: What the criterion scores, in the page's words.

criterion.description: The page's label for the criterion. A slot the page scores under a different name in each category carries a label that joins the names, as the page writes it; byCategory names each.

weightPercent.description: The criterion's share of the score, in percent; a rubric's weights sum to 100.

scoreMax.description: The highest score a criterion takes. Absent with scoreMin: the page publishes no score scale.

scoreMin.description: The lowest score a criterion takes. Absent with scoreMax: the page publishes no score scale.

source.description: The organizer's page the criteria were checked against.

otherSubmissionsOfRepo.description: Other stored submissions of the same repo, not reviewed here.

angles.description: Deterministic derivations from served facts: each names its evidence; not judgments.

fundedPeers.description: null when the idea maps to no vertical (not computed, never an empty list).

fundingBar.description: null when the idea maps to no vertical: nothing was counted, which is not zero funded projects.

fundedProjects.description: Every ACTIVE directory project in the vertical with an SCF award on record. fundedPeers lists only the 8 largest, so its length is not this count.

totalAwardedUSD.description: Recorded award USD across all fundedProjects, not just the listed peers.

source.description: unavailable = the live round check failed; open is [] but says nothing about actual round state.

vet.description: Same computation as /api/vet-idea: competitors, maturity, judged prior art, and the supply-side gap row.

matchMode.description: How relevance was established for the served projects: vertical = typed membership; vertical+scored = typed members plus rows that scored on the idea's own terms; scored = an anchor token matched; weak = generic words only (rows are neighbours, not evidence a competitor exists) or no project matched enough of the idea (projects is empty, which is not evidence that none exists). When the idea uses two or more words the directory knows, every served project matches a minimum share of their weight (rarer words weigh more), so fewer than 8 can be served.

status.description: The project's directory status, read live with this response; not dated per row.

via.description: How the row qualified: vertical = a typed member of the idea's vertical; scored = it matched the idea's own words. Absent when the idea maps to no vertical.

tier.description: The repo's grade tier, read live from the index with this response; not dated per row.

gap.description: SUPPLY-side coverage of the idea's vertical: a gap is not demand. Null when no vertical mapped.

builds.description: null = the submissions index could not be read (not checked; the note says so), [] = checked, none listed (read it with buildsBelowEvidenceRule). consumerFindings.description: Defects filed against this service by its largest agent consumer (stellar-raven), from THEIR evaluation battery. counts is their answer key; ourResponse is our own linked-issue state and is fenced off deliberately, a score computed from a variable we control is not an external grade.

counts.description: THEIR status vocabulary -> count, verbatim from their records.

blockedUpstream.description: Open rows a consumer we do not control decides.

refreshQueue.description: Open rows that are a refresh, not a defect: a note citing a version upstream has bumped, an archived repo with no recorded successor, a URL a probe proved dead. Counted apart so `open` stays a backlog someone can burn down.

states.description: The partition rule: open + refreshQueue + blockedUpstream + cleared + verified = total, disjoint.

flow.description: Findings as a node/link graph: detector -> surface -> outcome, whole-ledger counts (not a sample). nodes carry a column index (0 detector, 1 surface, 2 outcome) and a throughput value; links carry source/target node indexes and the count flowing between them.

gapMatrix.description: Entity x missing-field map with REAL identifiers: the actionable half of this report. Each row: what is missing, the count and denominator (a sample, never a census), why it matters to a caller, what closes it, and example slugs/repos so the gap can be worked or independently checked.

guards.description: Every guard with its promise and THREE-state verdict: holding (measured and passing on fresh evidence), breached (measured and failing), stale (evidence older than the guard's own freshness window; neither passing nor failing). holding is true ONLY in the holding state, so a stale guard is never green.

measure.description: The headline as numbers, so a consumer never parses prose. of is null for rates and bare counts.

knownLimitations.description: Read first. Each entry is derived from a measurement, not authored: what the limit IS, the number behind it, and what to do instead.

library.description: The written record behind the numbers: lesson write-ups per defect class, committed fetch receipts for human-verified corrections, and audit reports. Paths are repo-relative.

cachePolicy.description: How stale this response may legitimately be (cache + stale-while-revalidate). Read measuredAt, not the clock.

missFunnel.description: Where known-item misses die. Every open recall finding is replayed live and classified at the FIRST failing stage: passing (no longer reproduces) / ranking (returned but below top-3) / admission (not returned for the query) / identity (own exact name does not return it) / corpus (not in the directory at all). Stages are mutually exclusive and each names its owning area. A high 'passing' share means the open finding count is carrying STALE entries rather than real debt.

unclassified.description: Open recall findings whose probe shape this funnel cannot replay. Real findings the funnel is blind to, not cleared ones.

northStar.description: The one number the engine system optimizes (full-surface audit ok-rate), served WITH its age. warning is non-null whenever it should not be read as current (stale, below target, or a series measured over changing probe counts).

perOperation.description: Per-OPERATION contract quality, keyed by the operationId a caller invokes. contractProbe: clean (probe reached it, no violations) / violations (reached, listed) / skipped (could not check, reason given) / unmeasured (never reached). An unmeasured operation is NOT a passing one.

progress.description: Where this service stands against its own published quality plan (QUALITY.md). A phase cannot show done here without being done there, and remaining work is served with the same weight as finished work.

coverage.description: Coverage rates against the population each metric TARGETS. Two populations with different intent: the curated index (project-link + builder-owned rows a directory record claims) and the ec-taxonomy tail (indexed for completeness, scanned opportunistically, low coverage there is intended). Whole-census withCodeDepth/withNotes/withMainnet remain for continuity but carry no intent.

duplicateRows.description: Rows whose fullName duplicates another row. Storage debt, tracked here until zero; all counts are over DISTINCT repos.

thinnestEvidence.description: Indexed but thinly evidenced: the repo work queue.

deployable.description: the scanner marked this row a deployable contract

mainnetJoined.description: a verified mainnet contract is attributed to this repo (raw field mainnetContractId)

activity.description: Derived from lastCommitAt: active (<=90d) / slowing (<=365d) / dormant / archived. null = no commit date held; unknown is not dormant.

population.description: Total rows in the collection. read should equal it; the counts here are a census, not a sample.

weakestRows.description: The curation queue: each row's slug, evidence score, and exactly which facts are missing.

batteryErrors.description: Battery slices that CRASHED that day. A crashed slice is not a pass and not a fail; without this counter a crashed run rendered as a perfect green day.

answerAsOf.description: When the answer was true. NULL WHENEVER answerSource is 'deepwiki'. DeepWiki exposes no index date, so the age of such an answer is genuinely unknown and we will not invent one. Do NOT substitute codeVerified.scannedAt, codeVerified.scannedRef or repoMeta.lastCommitAt: those date OUR SOURCE SCAN, and a DeepWiki answer can be older than the scanned ref and contradict it (reported 2026-08-31: an answer said MaxSupportedProtocolVersion = 25 while the source at the scanned ref defined 28). Populated for answerSource 'knowledge-note' (the note's own verification asOf: day-granular, serialized as that day's 00:00:00Z; such notes now LEAD answers that name the exact identifier, precisely the reported class) and 'stellarlight-code-scan' (the answer IS the scan; scannedAt dates it). When null, verify any specific value against repoUrl at scannedRef.

answerSource.description: Where the answer text came from ('knowledge-note' | 'deepwiki' | 'stellarlight-code-scan'); null when no answer was produced; cite it alongside the answer. It states the GROUNDING, never the age: see answerAsOf. 'knowledge-note' = a curated, dated, source-cited fact that directly names the identifier asked about; it LEADS the answer, and any DeepWiki walkthrough appended after it is an undated index that can lag it; where they disagree, the dated fact wins.

answered.description: Always present, including when routedVia is null (then false).

codeVerified.description: Code-verified truth from analyzing the routed repo's ACTUAL source; qualify the answer with it: a deployable contract on a supported soroban-sdk is authoritative; tooling that merely uses Stellar is not. Null until code-scanned.

codeConfidence.description: Deterministic trust score for the code facts (basis code-scan × freshness of scannedAt). Null when never scanned.

contractInterfacePaths.description: The repo-relative source file of each contractInterface entry, same order and length: contractInterfacePaths[i] is where contractInterface[i] is defined at scannedRef. Interfaces in test code (tests/, __tests__/, fixtures/, testdata/, e2e/, fuzz targets, test helpers, suites and contracts, test wasm workspaces, test files such as foo_test.rs, and test contracts inside an integration/ folder) are left out of contractInterface; one under an examples or template folder is kept, and its path says so. Only contractInterface, symbols and sdkCapabilities leave test code out; stellarProof, codeDepth, isDeployableContract and stellarDeps still read every fetched file until a measured follow-up, so a repo whose only Soroban crate is a test fixture can serve an empty contractInterface beside a cargo-sdk proof. [] when the scan that recorded paths found no interface. null when no paths were recorded: the repo was scanned before 2026-11-04, and such a scan also read integration-test, testdata, e2e and test wasm folders, so an entry may be a test fixture until the next scan.

isDeployableContract.description: The routed repo's PRODUCT is a deployable Soroban contract. Known platform/SDK/tooling repos (stellar-core, rs-soroban-env, the SDKs/CLI/RPC…) are pinned FALSE: they vendor cdylib crates as runtime/fixtures, and this flag must never be read as 'Stellar Core itself is deployable'.

scannedRef.description: Commit SHA of the default branch the code facts were computed at; cite github.com/<fullName>/tree/<scannedRef>. Null on scans before 2026-08-12.

knowledgeNotes.description: Every public, curated, dated, source-cited fact StellarLight holds for the routed repo: deprecations, renames and moved paths, registry identity (npm / PyPI / crates / Maven names), release trains, security advisories, whether or not one of them led the answer. Empty when none are curated. Read these even when answerSource is 'deepwiki': a walkthrough describes mechanism; it never says the package is deprecated or the path moved. Each note cites its own source URL and carries its verification date.

warnings.description: THIS OPERATION ONLY: present on deepwiki-grounded answers, carrying the answer-dating disclaimer (answerAsOf is null; scannedAt/scannedRef/lastCommitAt date OUR SOURCE SCAN, not the answer). A reader that keeps only the first rows gets the best of every source, not the first sources named. Each row names its source. meta.bySource carries each source's status, returned count, matchMode, sourceDocCount and resultsHash. The rows are the single-source call's rows; scores can differ in the fourth decimal between any two calls that embed the query separately (two single-source calls on different instances do too), which can swap near-tied rows, so compare row ids across separate calls. status.description: HTTP status of this source's read (200 = answered). Not dated: it describes this response only.

matchMode.description: vector = similarity ranking over embeddings (conceptual, not literal keyword truth); keyword = vector search unavailable, coarse keyword match over title and content.

model.description: Embedding model used for vector retrieval (e.g. voyage-3); null in keyword mode.

query.description: The query as the server parsed it.

sourceEmpty.description: True when the `source` filter names a declared source that holds no documents yet. The page is an empty vector page (no keyword pass, no advisory): an empty source, not a miss. Drop the filter or pick another source.

Server-Timing.description: Our own wall time per phase in milliseconds (init, embed, vector, rank, total), so a consumer can split our time from transfer time.
